text: EX-10.3 6 tm2629827d1_ex10-3.htm EXHIBIT 10.3 Exhibit 10.3 November 13, 2026 BY EMAIL Sarah Wiltse [***] [***] Dear Sarah: As we have discussed, we are delighted that you will remain with Bright Horizon Energy (“ BHE ”) Corporation in the important role of Chief Human Resources Officer (“ CHRO ”) (or in such other executive level position as appointed by BHE) to lead the BHE human resources department following the merger. This letter agreement (the “ Transition Agreement ”) sets forth certain terms related to your continued service as CHRO of BHE as of the first day immediately following the closing of the merger (the “ Effective Date ”). Your Continued Employment After the Merger BHE agrees to continue your employment, and you accept continued employment with BHE, pursuant to the terms of this Transition Agreement commencing as of the Effective Date. You agree that immediately upon the termination of your employment with BHE for any reason, you shall resign from all positions you then hold as an officer, director or similar role of BHE or any of its affiliates, and in connection with any such resignation, you agree to execute such other documentation as is reasonably requested from BHE to reflect such resignation. Position, Duties, Authority and Responsibilities As of the Effective Date, you will be employed by BHE as its CHRO, an executive officer role reporting directly to BHE’s Chief Executive Officer, or in such other executive level position as BHE designates, with duties, authority and responsibilities consistent with the success profile agreed to you between you and BHE, and otherwise providing such duties consistent with your role as CHRO, or such other executive level position, as may be requested by BHE from time to time and following all applicable written policies and procedures adopted by BHE, including without limitation policies related to business ethics, conflict of interest, confidentiality and protection of trade secrets. Compensation During the two-year “Protection Period” (as defined in the Change in Control Agreement between you and Black Hills Corporation dated as of November 15, 2025 (the “CIC Agreement”)) that commences as of the closing of the merger, your total direct compensation (base salary, target short-term incentives and target long-term incentives) opportunities will be subject to review and adjustment by the BHE Compensation Committee, except that in no circumstances will your total direct compensation opportunities be reduced below your current total direct compensation opportunities without your express written agreement. www.blackhillsenergy.com “Good Reason” Termination The merger will be deemed to constitute a “Change in Control” for purposes of the CIC Agreement. The existing terms of your CIC Agreement will remain in place, except that the period to provide notice of termination for “Good Reason” (as defined in the CIC Agreement) in Section 8(c) of the CIC Agreement following the initial existence of a Good Reason condition will be the Protection Period. In addition to providing notice of the Good Reason termination, benefits under your CIC Agreement will only become payable to you in the event that you continue providing services to BHE until your successor commences employment with BHE. Accordingly, you must provide notice of your Good Reason termination during the Protection Period, but you may be required to remain employed beyond the Protection Period until your successor commences employment and such continued employment will not negate your ability to resign for Good Reason. The parties agree that, notwithstanding any other language in the Good Reason definition, your accepting the position of CHRO and entering into this Transition Agreement will constitute a Good Reason event for the duration of the Protection Period. Accordingly, you may exercise a Good Reason termination at any time during the Protection Period by providing a written Notice of Termination at least thirty (30) days prior to your Good Reason termination in accordance with the CIC Agreement (but with BHE having no right or ability to remedy you resigning for Good Reason based on the changes to your duties, authority and responsibilities as of the Effective Date) and receive the benefits identified in Section 9(b) of your CIC Agreement subject to your signing a Waiver and Release Agreement as required by your CIC Agreement and remaining employed until your successor commences employment. Notwithstanding the foregoing, and without limiting any rights under the CIC Agreement upon a without Cause termination, BHE may terminate you for Cause (as defined in the CIC Agreement) at any time, with respect to grounds arising prior to or following the Effective Date, and such termination for Cause will not trigger any severance payment obligations under the CIC Agreement but will result in the cessation of your right to terminate for Good Reason. Cooperation Following the termination of your employment with BHE for any reason, you will, upon reasonable request of BHE or its designee, consult with BHE regarding business matters that you were directly involved with while employed by BHE, and be reasonably available, with or without subpoena, to be interviewed, review documents or things, give depositions, testify, or engage in other reasonable activities in connection with any litigation or investigation, with respect to matters that you then have or may have knowledge of by virtue of your employment by or service to BHE. In connection with such cooperation requested by BHE or its designee, BHE shall reimburse you for any reasonable out-of-pocket costs incurred as a result of your compliance with such cooperation obligations but will not compensate you for any reasonable time you spend cooperating in accordance with this provision. Covenants Protection of Confidential Information The term “ Confidential Information ”, for purposes of this Transition Agreement, includes all information and material, whether in written, electronic, or oral form, or any other form whatsoever, that is proprietary and has not been publicly disclosed by BHE, including BHE’s trade secrets. Confidential Information includes but is not limited to: (a) non-public documents and personally private information regarding (i) BHE’s employees (identifying information, protected health information, salary/incentive pay structure and information, performance evaluations); (ii) contract counterparties; and, (iii) transactions with counterparties, including information that is provided to BHE that is subject to obligations of confidentiality; (b) business plans and strategies, records of financial performance, methods of operation, budgets, sales or forecasts; (c) competitive analyses, engineering plans or drawings, training materials; (d) pricing information and costs or projected costs; (e) bids or proposals, and contract arrangements with counterparties, including specific terms of such arrangements; and (f) financial statements, analyses, reports and positions, that are not publicly disclosed. Subject to the Permissible Conduct provision below, y ou agree that you will use Confidential Information only for purposes of performing your duties for BHE, within the course and scope of your employment with BHE, and that you will not use or disclose any Confidential Information, in whole or in part, for any other purpose. You agree to keep confidential all Confidential Information and to preserve the confidential and proprietary nature of the Confidential Information at all times, even following the termination of your employment with BHE for any reason, whether voluntary or involuntary. You will not, directly or indirectly, copy, take or remove from BHE’s premises or from secure electronic information systems and hardware any Confidential Information. Non-Solicitation You agree that during your employment with BHE and for a period of twenty-four (24) consecutive months immediately following the termination of your employment for any reason, whether at the initiative of you or BHE, you will not directly or indirectly, on your own behalf or on the behalf of any other individual or entity: (a) solicit the employment of any employee of BHE, on behalf of yourself or any other individual or entity, or otherwise interfere with the employment relationship between any such employee and BHE; or (b) induce any of BHE’s agents, representatives, consultants, contractors or customers with whom you had access during your employment with BHE, and who are located or do business within Pennington County, provided that BHE continues to carry on a like business within that area, to terminate or alter their relationship with BHE. Permissible Conduct Nothing in this Transition Agreement prohibits you from reporting possible violations of state or federal law or regulations to any governmental agency or entity, including but not limited to the Department of Justice, the Securities and Exchange Commission, the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission, or the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, or from making other disclosures that are protected under the whistleblower provisions of applicable law. In addition, nothing in this Transition Agreement precludes you from participating in government investigations or inquiries relating to BHE or engaging in other activities specifically protected under applicable law. You are not required to notify or seek permission from BH prior to engaging in any of the foregoing activities. Notwithstanding any other provisions of this Transition Agreement, you understand that you may not be held criminally or civilly liable under any federal or state trade secret law for the disclosure of a trade secret that is made (i) in confidence to a federal, state or local government official, either directly or indirectly, or to an attorney if such disclosure is made solely for the purpose of reporting or investigating a suspected violation of law or for pursuing an anti-retaliation lawsuit; or (ii) in a complaint or other document filed in a lawsuit or other proceeding, if such filing is made under seal and you do not disclose the trade secret except pursuant to a court order, in each case, in accordance with 18 U.S.C. §§ 1833(b)(1) and 1833(b)(2). Reasonable Restrictions and Notice Obligation You have carefully read and considered the covenants above and, having done so, agree that the restrictions set forth above, including the time periods of such restrictions, are reasonable and are reasonably required for the protection of the legitimate business interests of BHE. You agree that such covenants are necessary and designed to protect BHE’s trade secrets and other important business interests. You further agree that while employed by BHE and for twenty-four (24) months thereafter, you will communicate the content of the covenants above to any individual, entity or association with which you intend to be employed, become associated or to represent. Injunctive Relief You acknowledges that the interests of BHE would be irreparably harmed, and the remedy at law available to BHE for your breach of any obligation under this Transition Agreement would be inadequate. You agree that, in addition to any other remedy available at law or in equity, BHE may be granted temporary or permanent injunctive relief in any proceeding brought to enforce any provision of this Transition Agreement or to prevent the actual or threatened disclosure of Confidential Information, without necessity of proof of actual damage, and without posting a bond. Miscellaneous Except as expressly otherwise provided herein and in the CIC Agreement, this Transition Agreement contains the complete, entire understanding of the parties to this Transition Agreement related to your continued employment with BHE. In executing this Transition Agreement, no party relies on any term, condition, promise or representation other than those expressed in this Transition Agreement. This Transition Agreement supersedes and replaces entirely all prior and contemporaneous oral and written agreements and discussions with respect to the subject matter of this Transition Agreement, except for the CIC Agreement (except as modified by this Transition Agreement); provided, however, that nothing in this Transition Agreement supersedes or replaces any of the terms of any BHE policy, which remains in effect in accordance with their terms. This Transition Agreement may be amended or modified only by an agreement in writing signed by you and an authorized officer of BHE. This Transition Agreement shall be fully binding upon any successor or assign (whether direct or indirect, by purchase, merger, consolidation or otherwise) to the business and/or assets of BHE, in the same manner and to the same extent that BHE would be obligated under this Transition Agreement. In the case of any transaction in which a successor or assign would not by the foregoing provision, or by operation of law, be bound by this Transition Agreement, BHE shall require such successor or assign to expressly and unconditionally assume and agree to perform all the obligations of BHE under this Transition Agreement, in the same manner and to the same extent that BHE would be required to perform it if no such succession or assignment had taken place. Any failure to obtain such assumption and continuation of this Transition Agreement shall constitute a material breach hereof. Neither this Transition Agreement nor any right or interest hereunder shall be assignable or transferable by you, your beneficiaries or legal representatives, except by will or by the laws of descent and distribution. This Transition Agreement shall inure to the benefit of and be enforceable by your legal personal representative. Notwithstanding anything in this Transition Agreement or any written or unwritten policy of BHE to the contrary, if it shall be determined that any payment or distribution by BHE to or for your benefit, whether paid or payable or distributed or distributable pursuant to the terms of this Transition Agreement, any other agreement between you and BHE or an affiliate (a “ Payment ” or “ Payments ”), would constitute a parachute payment (“ Parachute Payment ”) within the meaning of Section 280G of the Internal Revenue Code (the “ Code ”) and would, but for this paragraph , be subject to the excise tax imposed under Section 4999 of the Code (or any successor provision thereto) or any similar tax imposed by state or local law, together with any interest or penalties imposed with respect to such excise taxes (collectively, the “ Excise Tax ”), then prior to making the Payments, a calculation shall be made comparing (i) the Net Benefit (as defined below) to you of the Payments after payment of the Excise Tax to (ii) the Net Benefit to you if the Payments are reduced to the extent necessary to avoid being subject to the Excise Tax. Only if the amount calculated under (i) above is less than the amount under (ii) above will the Payments be reduced to the minimum extent necessary to ensure that no portion of the Payments is subject to the Excise Tax. “ Net Benefit ” shall mean the present value of the Payments net of all federal, state, local, foreign income, employment and excise taxes, determined in accordance with Section 280G(d)(4). The Payments shall be reduced in a manner that maximizes your economic position. In applying this principle, the reduction shall be made in a manner consistent with the requirements of Section 409A of the Code, and where two economically equivalent amounts are subject to reduction but payable at different times, such amounts shall be reduced on a pro rata basis but not below zero. Any determination required under this paragraph , including whether any payments or benefits constitute a Parachute Payment, shall be made by an independent certified public accounting firm (the “ Accounting Firm ”) retained by BHE. You shall provide BHE with such information and documents as BHE may reasonably request in order to make a determination under this paragraph . BHE’s determination shall be final and binding on you. The parties acknowledge that you are solely responsible for the payment of any Excise Tax that is assessed based upon a Parachute Payment made pursuant to this Transition Agreement or any other Parachute Payment made by BHE or an affiliate pursuant to any other plan or obligation. As a result of the uncertainty in the application of Sections 280G and 4999 of the Code at the time of the initial determination by the Accounting Firm, however, it is possible that amounts will have been paid or distributed to you or for your benefit which should not have been so paid or distributed (an “ Overpayment ”) or that additional amounts which shall not have been paid or distributed to you or for your benefit should have been so paid or distributed (an “ Underpayment ”), in each case, consistent with the calculation of the amount. If the Accounting Firm, based either upon the assertion of a deficiency by the Internal Revenue Service against you or BHE which the Accounting Firm believes has a high probability of success or controlling precedent or other substantial authority, determines that an Overpayment has been made, any such Overpayment must be treated (if permitted by applicable law) for all purposes as a loan ab initio for which you must repay BHE together with interest at the applicable federal rate under Section 7872(f)(2) of the Code; provided, however, that no such loan may be deemed to have been made and no amount shall be payable by you to BHE if and to the extent that such deemed loan and payment would not either reduce the amount on which you are subject to tax under Section 4999 of the Code or generate a refund of such taxes. If the Accounting Firm, based upon controlling precedent or other substantial authority, determines that an Underpayment has occurred, the independent third party expert must promptly notify BHE of the amount of the Underpayment and such amount, together with interest at the applicable federal rate under Section 7872(f)(2) of the Code, must be paid to you. This Transition Agreement is intended to comply with the requirements of applicable law, including Section 409A of the Code, or an exemption thereto. Any amounts that may become payable pursuant to this Transition Agreement may only be made to you upon an event and in a manner permitted by Section 409A of the Code, to the extent applicable. Separation pay provided pursuant to this Transition Agreement is intended to be exempt from Section 409A of the Code under the “separation pay” and/or “short-term deferral” exceptions to the maximum permissible extent. If you are considered a “specified employee,” if and to the extent necessary to comply with Section 409A of the Code, any payments due to you shall be delayed for a period of six months after your separation from service. Any payment due to you shall be treated as a separate payment for purposes of Section 409A of the Code. In no event may you, directly or indirectly, designate the calendar year of a payment. If the period for executing a release spans two calendar years and the amounts payable to you are subject to Section 409A of the Code, payment of any amounts to you in connection with the execution of the release shall be made in the second calendar year. BHE makes no representation or warranty with respect to tax consequences of this Transition Agreement, and BHE shall have no liability to you or any other person for any taxes or penalties imposed pursuant to Section 409A of the Code. This Transition Agreement is governed by and will be construed and enforced in accordance with the laws of the State of South Dakota. ***** On behalf of BHE, I thank you for all of your past contributions to BHE and look forward to working with you. Sincerely, /s/ Linden Evans Linden Evans, President and Chief Executive Officer ACKNOWLEDGED AND AGREED: /s/ Sarah Wiltse Name: Sarah Wiltse Date: 11/13/2026

text: EX-10.1 2 aqb-20261110xex10_1.htm EX-10.1 Exhibit 10.1 Univest Termination Agreement Exhibit 10. 1 TERMINATION AGREEMENT This TERMINATION AGREEMENT (this “Agreement”) is made and entered into as of November 13 , 2026, by and between AquaBounty Technologies, Inc., a Delaware corporation (“AQB”), and Univest Securities, LLC, a Delaware limited liability company (“Univest” and together with AQB, the “Parties,” and each, a “Party”). RECITALS WHEREAS, AQB and Univest entered into (i) that certain Placement Agency Agreement, dated October 28, 2025 (the “October 2025 PAA”), pursuant to which Univest acted as exclusive placement agent in connection with AQB’s offering of senior notes, (ii) that certain Placement Agency Agreement, dated April 7, 2026 (the “April 2026 PAA”), pursuant to which Univest acted as exclusive placement agent in connection with AQB’s exchange of certain outstanding notes for shares of Series A Convertible Preferred Stock and the private placement of such securities for cash, and (iii) that certain Placement Agency Agreement, dated June 25, 2026 , pursuant to which Univest acted as placement agent in connection with AQB’s private placement for cash of shares of Series B Convertible Preferred Stock (the “June 2026 PAA” and, together with the October 2025 PAA and the April 2026 PAA, the “Placement Agency Agreements,” and each, a “Placement Agency Agreement”) ; WHEREAS, AQB and Univest Group, Inc. , a Nevada corporation and holder of all of the outstanding membership interests of Univest, contemplate entering into a binding letter of intent and definitive agreements relating to a proposed business combination transaction pursuant to which Univest would become a n indirect wholly owned subsidiary of AQB, and following such transaction, AQB is expected to complete a substantially concurrent private placement of certain securities (collectively, the “Proposed Transaction”); and WHEREAS, in contemplation of the Proposed Transaction, the Parties desire to terminate the Placement Agency Agreements and to terminate and waive the Right of First Refusal and the other continuing rights of Univest under each Placement Agency Agreement as set forth herein. AGREEMENTS NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the premises set forth above and other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the Parties agree as follows: 1. Termination of Historical Arrangements. Effective immediately upon execution and delivery of this Agreement by all Parties (the “Effective Time”): (a) t he right of first refusal under each of Section 10 of the October 2025 PAA, Section 4(m) of the April 2026 PAA and Section 4(m) of the June 2026 PAA (each and collectively, the “Right of First Refusal”), and all other continuing exclusivity, participation, advisory, notice, matching and similar rights under each Placement Agency Agreement, are hereby irrevocably terminated, extinguished and waived in all respects; and (b) each Placement Agency Agreement, and all placement agency, exclusive engagement and other arrangements under or contemplated by any placement agency agreement between the Parties (whether or not specifically identified herein), are hereby terminated and, except as expressly preserved by this Agreement, shall be of no further force or effect, and Univest shall not be deemed to be acting as placement agent, broker, financial advisor or investment banker to AQB in connection with any current or future transaction. 2. Accrued Fees, Expenses and Indemnification. Except as expressly set forth herein, all rights to future fees, commissions and expense reimbursement under each Placement Agency Agreement shall terminate at the Effective Time. Any fees actually earned and payable and expenses actually incurred and reimbursable through the Effective Time shall survive. The confidentiality, indemnification and contribution provisions of each Placement Agency Agreement, to the extent applicable, shall survive solely with respect to services performed and matters arising through the Effective Time; provided that no surviving provision shall preserve or revive any exclusivity, Right of First Refusal, participation, advisory, notice, matching or similar right terminated under this Agreement. 3. Representations and Warranties. Each Party hereby represents and warrants to the other Party that: (a) it has the full right, power, and authority to enter into and perform this Agreement and the obligations hereunder; (b) the execution, delivery and performance of this Agreement have been duly authorized by all necessary action on the part of such Party ; (c) this Agreement constitutes the legal, valid , and binding obligation of such Party , enforceable against such Party in accordance with its terms, subject to applicable bankruptcy, insolvency and similar laws and general equitable principles; and (d) it has not assigned or transferred any right terminated or waived by it under this Agreement , except as disclosed in writing to the other Party before execution. 4. Further Assurances. Each Party shall execute and deliver such additional documents and take such further actions as may be reasonably necessary to implement the termination, consent, waiver and release contemplated by this Agreement. 5. Miscellaneous. (a) Governing Law; Jurisdiction; Waiver of Jury Trial . This Agreement shall be deemed to have been made and delivered in New York City, and this Agreement and the transactions contemplated hereby shall be governed as to validity, interpretation, construction, effect and in all other respects by the internal laws of the State of New York, without regard to the conflict-of-laws principles thereof. Each Party: (i) agrees that any legal suit, action or proceeding arising out of or relating to this Agreement or the transactions contemplated hereby shall be instituted exclusively in the New York Supreme Court, County of New York, or in the United States District Court for the Southern District of New York; (ii) waives any objection that such Party may now or hereafter have to the venue of any such suit, action or proceeding; and (iii) irrevocably consents to the jurisdiction of such courts in any such suit, action or proceeding. Each Party further agrees to accept and acknowledge service of any and all process that may be served in any such suit, action or proceeding in the New York Supreme Court, County of New York, or in the United States District Court for the Southern District of New York, and agrees that service of process upon such Party mailed by certified mail to such Party’s address set forth herein shall be deemed in every respect effective service of process upon such Party in any such suit, action or proceeding. Nothing contained herein shall be deemed to limit in any way any right to serve process in any other manner permitted by applicable law. Each Party hereby irrevocably waives, to the fullest extent permitted by applicable law, any and all right to trial by jury in any legal proceeding arising out of or relating to this Agreement or the transactions contemplated hereby. (b) Entire Agreement . This Agreement constitutes the entire agreement of the Parties and supersedes all prior written or oral, and all contemporaneous oral, agreements, understandings and negotiations between the Parties with respect to the subject matter hereof. In the event of any conflict between this Agreement and any Placement Agency Agreement with respect to the rights terminated or waived pursuant to this Agreement, this Agreement shall control. (c) Amendments and Waivers . This Agreement may not be amended, modified or supplemented except by a written instrument signed by each Party. No provision of this Agreement may be waived except by a written instrument signed by the Party against whom the waiver is to be enforced. No waiver of any provision of this Agreement shall constitute a waiver of any other provision or a continuing waiver of the provision so waived. (d) Assignment . Neither this Agreement nor any of the rights, interests or obligations hereunder may be assigned by any Party without the prior written consent of the other Party, and any purported assignment in violation of this provision shall be null and void. Subject to the foregoing, this Agreement shall be binding upon and inure to the benefit of the Parties and their respective successors and permitted assigns. (e) No Third-Party Beneficiaries . N othing in this Agreement, express or implied, is intended to or shall confer upon any Person other than the Parties and their respective successors and permitted assigns any legal or equitable right, benefit or remedy of any nature whatsoever under or by reason of this Agreement. “Person” means any individual, corporation, partnership, limited liability company, association, trust or other entity. (f) Severability . If any term or provision of this Agreement is determined to be invalid, illegal or unenforceable in any jurisdiction, such invalidity, illegality or unenforceability shall not affect any other term or provision of this Agreement or invalidate or render unenforceable such term or provision in any other jurisdiction. Upon such determination, the Parties shall negotiate in good faith to modify this Agreement so as to effect the original intent of the Parties as closely as possible in an acceptable manner. (g) Expenses . Except as otherwise expressly provided in this Agreement, each Party shall bear its own fees, costs and expenses incurred in connection with the negotiation, preparation, execution and performance of this Agreement and the transactions contemplated hereby. (h) Counterparts; Electronic Signatures . This Agreement may be executed in two or more counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original, but all of which, when taken together, shall constitute one and the same agreement. Signatures delivered by facsimile transmission, electronic mail in portable document format or other electronic means shall have the same force and effect as manually executed original signatures. (i) Headings . The headings contained in this Agreement are for convenience of reference only and shall not affect the construction or interpretation of this Agreement. (j) Construction . The Parties have participated jointly in the negotiation and drafting of this Agreement. If an ambiguity or question of intent or interpretation arises, this Agreement shall be construed as if drafted jointly by the Parties, and no presumption or burden of proof shall arise favoring or disfavoring any Party by virtue of the authorship of any provision of this Agreement. text: EX-10.1 2 ex10-1.htm EX-10.1 Exhibit 10.1 MUTUAL TERMINATION AGREEMENT This Mutual Termination Agreement (this “Termination Agreement”) is entered into as of November 11, 2026, by and among: 1. Addentax Group Corp., a corporation incorporated under the laws of the State of Nevada, United States of America (the “Company”); 2. Yingxi Industrial Chain Investment Co., Ltd., a company incorporated under the laws of Hong Kong and a wholly-owned subsidiary of the Company (“Yingxi”); 3. Double Cash Finance Limited, a company incorporated under the laws of Hong Kong (“Double Cash Finance”); and 4. Mr. Chan Kai Sang, the sole shareholder of Double Cash Finance (the “Shareholder”). The above parties are collectively referred to as the “Parties.” RECITALS WHEREAS, the Parties entered into a Share Exchange Agreement dated November 3, 2026 (the “Original Agreement”), pursuant to which Yingxi agreed to acquire 100% of the issued and outstanding shares of Double Cash Finance in exchange for the issuance of 464,907 shares of common stock of the Company; WHEREAS, the transactions contemplated under the Original Agreement have not been consummated; and WHEREAS, the Parties have mutually agreed to terminate the Original Agreement. NOW, THEREFORE, the Parties hereby agree as follows: 1. Termination Effective as of the date of this Termination Agreement, the Original Agreement is hereby terminated in its entirety and shall have no further force or effect. 2. Release of Obligations Upon termination of the Original Agreement, each Party shall be released from its respective obligations under the Original Agreement, and no Party shall have any further obligation to consummate the transactions contemplated thereunder. 3. No Termination Fee The Parties agree that no termination fee, penalty or other compensation shall be payable by any Party in connection with the termination of the Original Agreement. 4. Mutual Release Each Party hereby releases and discharges the other Parties from any and all claims, liabilities and obligations arising out of or relating to the Original Agreement, except for obligations expressly provided under this Termination Agreement. 5. Governing Law and Jurisdiction (a) THIS TERMINATION AGREEMENT SHALL BE GOVERNED IN ALL RESPECTS, INCLUDING AS TO VALIDITY, INTERPRETATION AND EFFECT, BY THE LAWS OF THE STATE OF NEW YORK, UNITED STATES OF AMERICA. (b) The Parties agree to submit to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of the State of New York or the Southern District of New York, as applicable. 6. Counterparts This Termination Agreement may be executed in counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original, and all of which together shall constitute one and the same instrument. IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the Parties have executed this Termination Agreement as of the date first written above. Addentax Group Corp. text: EX-10.1 2 ex10-1.htm EX-10.1 Exhibit 10.1 CONVERSION AND EXCHANGE AGREEMENT THIS CONVERSION AND EXCHANGE AGREEMENT (the “Agreement”), dated as of November ____, 2026, is made by and between Our Bond, Inc., a Nevada corporation (the “Company”), and the holder of Series B Preferred Stock of the Company signatory hereto (the “Holder”). WHEREAS, the Holder currently holds shares of the Company’s Series B-1, B-2, and/or B-3 Preferred Stock in the classes and denominations set forth on Schedule A hereto (collectively, the “Preferred Stock”); and WHEREAS, subject to the terms and conditions set forth in this Agreement and pursuant to Section 3(a)(9) of the Securities Act of 1933, as amended (the “Securities Act”), the Holder desires to convert the Preferred stock solely to shares of the Company’s common stock, $0.0001 par value per share (the “Common Stock”), NOW, THEREFORE, IN CONSIDERATION of the mutual covenants contained in this Agreement and for good and valuable consideration, the receipt and adequacy of which are hereby acknowledged, the Company and Holder agree as follows: 1. Terms of the Conversion and Exchange . The Company and Holder agree that the Holder will convert and exchange the Preferred Stock to shares of Common Stock (the “Conversion Shares”) at a ratio determined by dividing the total stated value of the Preferred Stock by a conversion price of $2.03 per share of Common Stock (the “Conversion Price”), to be issued per the order of the the Holder as shown on Schedule A hereto, and will relinquish any and all other rights it may have as a holder of the Preferred Stock, in exchange for the Conversion Shares. 2. Closing. Upon satisfaction of the conditions set forth herein, a closing shall occur at the principal offices of the Company, or such other location as the parties shall mutually agree. At closing, the Holder shall deliver instructions returning the Preferred Stock for cancellation and the Company shall cause its transfer agent to validly issue the Conversion Shares to the Holder in book entry form. 3. Further Assurances Each party shall do and perform, or cause to be done and performed, all such further acts and things, and shall execute and deliver all such other agreements, certificates, instruments and documents, as the other party may reasonably request in order to carry out the intent and accomplish the purposes of this Agreement and the consummation of the transactions contemplated hereby. 4. Representations and Warranties of the Holder. The Holder represents and warrants, as of the date hereof and as of the closing, to the Company as follows: a. Authorization; Enforcement . The Holder has the requisite power and authority to enter into and to consummate the transactions contemplated by this Agreement and otherwise to carry out its obligations hereunder and thereunder. The execution and delivery of this Agreement by the Holder and the consummation by it of the transactions contemplated hereby have been duly authorized by all necessary action on the part of the Holder and no further action is required by the Holder. This Agreement has been (or upon delivery will have been) duly executed by the Holder and, when delivered in accordance with the terms hereof, will constitute the valid and binding obligation of the Holder enforceable against the Holder in accordance with its terms, except: (i) as limited by general equitable principles and applicable bankruptcy, insolvency, reorganization, moratorium and other laws of general application affecting enforcement of creditors’ rights generally, (ii) as limited by laws relating to the availability of specific performance, injunctive relief or other equitable remedies and (iii) insofar as indemnification and contribution provisions may be limited by applicable law. 1 b. Tax Advisors . The Holder has reviewed with its own tax advisors the U.S. federal, state, local and foreign tax consequences of this the transactions contemplated by this Agreement. With respect to such matters, the Holder relies solely on such advisors and not on any statements or representations of the Company or any of its agents, written or oral. The Holder understands that it (and not the Company) shall be responsible for its own tax liability that may arise as a result of the transactions contemplated by this Agreement. c. Information Regarding Holder . Holder is an “accredited investor”, as such term is defined in Rule 501 of Regulation D promulgated by the United States Securities and Exchange Commission (the “Commission”) under the Securities Act, is experienced in investments and business matters, has made investments of a speculative nature and has purchased securities of companies in private placements in the past and, with its representatives, has such knowledge and experience in financial, tax and other business matters as to enable the Holder to utilize the information made available by the Company to evaluate the merits and risks of, and to make an informed investment decision with respect to, the proposed share exchange. 5. Rule 144 Matters . The parties acknowledge and agree that the exchange of the Preferred Stock for the Conversion Shares is being completed in accordance with Section 3(a)(9) of the Securities Act. The Company acknowledges that the holding period of the Conversion Shares may be tacked on to the holding period of the Preferred Stock for purposes of Rule 144 under the Securities Act. The Company agrees not to take a position contrary to this Section 5. 6. Representations and Warranties of the Company . The Company hereby makes the following representations and warranties to the Holder: a. Authorization; Enforcement . The Company has the requisite corporate power and authority to enter into and to consummate the transactions contemplated by this Agreement and otherwise to carry out its obligations hereunder. The execution and delivery of this Agreement by the Company and the consummation by the Company of the transactions contemplated hereby have been duly authorized by all necessary action on the part of the Company, and no further action is required by the Company or the Board of Directors of the Company in connection therewith. This Agreement has been (or upon delivery will have been) duly executed by the Company and, when delivered in accordance with the terms hereof, will constitute the valid and binding obligation of the Company enforceable against the Company in accordance with its terms, except: (i) as limited by general equitable principles and applicable bankruptcy, insolvency, reorganization, moratorium and other laws of general application affecting enforcement of creditors’ rights generally, and (ii) as limited by laws relating to the availability of specific performance, injunctive relief or other equitable remedies. b. Organization and Qualification . The Company is a corporation duly incorporated, validly existing, and in good standing under the laws of the State of Nevada and has the requisite power and authority to own its properties and to carry on its business as now being conducted and as presently proposed to be conducted. c. No Conflict . The execution, delivery and performance of this Agreement by the Company and the consummation by the Company of the transactions contemplated hereby will not (i) result in a violation of the Articles of Incorporation or other organizational documents of the Company, (ii) conflict with, or constitute a default (or an event which with notice or lapse of time or both would become a default) under, or give to others any rights of termination, amendment, acceleration or cancellation of, any agreement, indenture or instrument to which the Company is a party, or (iii) result in a violation of any law, rule, regulation, order, judgment or decree, or any of the regulations and the rules and regulations of principal market in which the Company’s securities are listed (the “Principal Market”), that are applicable to the Company or by which any property or asset of the Company is bound or affected. 2 d. No Consents . The Company is not required to obtain any consent from, authorization or order of, or make any filing or registration with, any court, governmental agency or any regulatory or self-regulatory agency in order for it to execute, deliver or perform any of its obligations under this Agreement. All consents, authorizations, orders, filings and registrations which the Company is required to obtain pursuant to the preceding sentence have been obtained or effected on or prior to the date of this Agreement. e. Securities Law Exemptions . Assuming the accuracy of the representations and warranties of the Holder contained herein, the issuance by the Company of the Conversion Shares is exempt from registration under the Securities Act. The Company covenants and represents to the Holder that the Company has not received, does not anticipate receiving, has not made any agreement to receive, and has been given any promise to receive, any consideration from the Holder or any other person in connection with the transactions contemplated by this Agreement as except as set forth herein. f. Issuance of Conversion Shares . The issuance of the Conversion Shares is duly authorized and upon issuance in accordance with the terms of this Agreement, the Conversion Shares shall be validly issued, fully paid and non-assessable shares of common stock in the Company free from all preemptive or similar rights, taxes, liens, charges and other encumbrances with respect to the issue thereof, with the Holder being entitled to all rights accorded to a holder of Common Stock in the Company. g. Company Status . The Company is not an issuer identified in Rule 144(i)(1) under the Securities Act. The Company is, and has been for a period of at least 90 days, subject to the reporting requirements of Section 13 or Section 15(d) of the Exchange Act. 7. Nasdaq Listing Rule 5635 Compliance . a. Nasdaq Rule 5635(d) . If, and only if, the Conversion Price is less than the Nasdaq Minimum Price (as defined in Nasdaq Listing Rule 5635(d)), as determined on the date this Agreement is executed and delivered, then, the Company shall not immediately issue Conversion Shares to the Holder to the extent that the total number of Conversion Shares issued upon all conversions of the Preferred Stock at a Conversion Price below the Nasdaq Minimum price would exceed 19.99% of the Company’s total issued and outstanding Common Stock immediately after such conversions (the “Exchange Cap”). In the event that the Exchange Cap is applicable: (i) the Holder shall be immediately issued its pro rata portion of the Conversion Shares issuable by the Company below the Exchange Cap; (ii) the Company shall employ its best efforts to obtain shareholder approval to issue Conversion Shares in excess of the Exchange Cap; and (iii) immediately upon the effective date of such shareholder approval, as obtained in accordance with the applicable Nasdaq Listing Rules, the Company shall issue all remaining Conversion Shares issuable to the Holder under this Agreement. b. Nasdaq Rule 5635(b). If, and only if, the Conversion Shares, when aggregated with any other shares of common stock of the Company beneficially owned by the Holder, would exceed twenty percent (20%) of the Company’s total issued and outstanding common stock immediately following transactions contemplated by this Agreement, then, the Company shall not immediately issue Conversion Shares to the Holder to the extent that the total number of Conversion Shares issued to the Holder would exceed 19.99% of the Company’s total issued and outstanding Common Stock immediately after such conversions (the “Control Cap”). In the event that the Control Cap is applicable: (i) the Holder shall be immediately issued its that portion of the Conversion Shares issuable by the Company to the Holder below the Control Cap; (ii) the Company shall employ its best efforts to obtain shareholder approval to issue Conversion Shares in excess of the Control Cap; and (iii) immediately upon the effective date of such shareholder approval, as obtained in accordance with the applicable Nasdaq Listing Rules, the Company shall issue all remaining Conversion Shares issuable to the Holder under this Agreement. 3 8. Miscellaneous . a. Successors and Assigns . This Agreement shall be binding upon and inure to the benefit of the parties and their respective successors and assigns. b. Governing Law; Jurisdiction; Waiver of Jury Trial . This Agreement shall be governed by and construed under the laws of the State of Nevada without regard to the choice of law principles thereof. Each party hereby irrevocably submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts sitting in the State of Nevada for the adjudication of any dispute hereunder or in connection herewith or therewith or with any transaction contemplated hereby or thereby, and hereby irrevocably waives any objection that such suit, action or proceeding is brought in an inconvenient forum or that the venue of such suit, action or proceeding is improper. Nothing contained herein shall be deemed to limit in any way any right to serve process in any manner permitted by law. EACH PARTY HEREBY IRREVOCABLY WAIVES ANY RIGHT IT MAY HAVE, AND AGREES NOT TO REQUEST, A JURY TRIAL FOR THE ADJUDICATION OF ANY DISPUTE HEREUNDER OR IN CONNECTION WITH OR ARISING OUT OF THIS AGREEMENT OR ANY TRANSACTION CONTEMPLATED HEREBY. c. Severability . If any provision of this Agreement shall be invalid or unenforceable in any jurisdiction, such invalidity or unenforceability shall not affect the validity or enforceability of the remainder of this Agreement in that jurisdiction or the validity or enforceability of any provision of this Agreement in any other jurisdiction. d. Counterparts/Execution . This Agreement may be executed in two or more identical counterparts, all of which shall be considered one and the same agreement and shall become effective when counterparts have been signed by each party and delivered to the other party. In the event that any signature is delivered by facsimile transmission or by an e-mail which contains an electronic file of an executed signature page, such signature page shall create a valid and binding obligation of the party executing (or on whose behalf such signature is executed) with the same force and effect as if such facsimile or electronic file signature page (as the case may be) were an original thereof. e. Expenses . Except as otherwise provided for herein, the parties hereto shall pay their own costs and expenses in connection herewith. f. Entire Agreement; Amendments . This Agreement constitutes the entire agreement between the parties with regard to the subject matter hereof and thereof, superseding all prior agreements or understandings, whether written or oral, between or among the parties. This Agreement may be amended, modified, superseded, cancelled, renewed or extended, and the terms and conditions hereof may be waived, only by a written instrument signed by all parties, or, in the case of a waiver, by the party waiving compliance. Except as expressly stated herein, no delay on the part of any party in exercising any right, power or privilege hereunder shall operate as a waiver thereof, nor shall any waiver on the part of any party of any right, power or privilege hereunder preclude any other or future exercise of any other right, power or privilege hereunder. g. Headings . The headings used in this Agreement are used for convenience only and are not to be considered in construing or interpreting this Agreement. text: EX-10.2 3 ex10-2.htm EX-10.2 Exhibit 10.2 November ___, 2026 Our Bond, Inc. 85 Broad Street New York, NY 10004 Re: Our Bond, Inc. - Lock-Up Agreement Ladies and Gentlemen: This Lock-Up Agreement is being delivered to you in connection with the Conversion and Exchange Agreement (the “ Conversion Agreement ”) by and among Our Bond, Inc. (the “ Company ”) and the shareholder of the Company signatory thereto (the “ Holder ”). Lock-Up Provisions The Holder agrees that, commencing on the date hereof and ending on the six-month anniversary of this Lock-Up Agreement (the “ Lock-Up Period ”), the Holder will not, and will cause all affiliates (as defined in Rule 144 promulgated under the Securities Act) of the Holder or any person in privity with the Holder or any affiliate of the Holder not to, directly or indirectly (i) sell, offer to sell, contract or agree to sell, hypothecate, pledge, grant any option to purchase, make any short sale or otherwise dispose of or agree to dispose of, directly or indirectly, any shares of common stock of the Company issued pursuant to the Conversion Agreement (the “ Conversion Shares ”), or establish or increase a put equivalent position or liquidate or decrease a call equivalent position within the meaning of Section 16 of the Exchange Act, as amended and the rules and regulations of the Securities and Exchange Commission (the “ SEC ”) promulgated thereunder with respect to any Conversion Shares owned directly by the Holder (including holding as a custodian) or with respect to which the Holder has beneficial ownership within the rules and regulations of the SEC (collectively, the “ Holder’s Conversion Shares ”), or (ii) enter into any swap or other arrangement that transfers to another, in whole or in part, any of the economic consequences of ownership of any of the Holder’s Conversion Shares, whether any such transaction described in clause (i) or (ii) above is to be settled by delivery of Conversion Shares, in cash or otherwise, (iii) make any demand for or exercise any right or cause to be filed a registration statement, including any amendments thereto, with respect to the registration of any Conversion Shares or (iv) publicly disclose the intention to do any of the foregoing. The foregoing restriction is expressly agreed to preclude the Holder, and any affiliate of the Holder, and any person in privity with the Holder or any affiliate of the Holder, from engaging in any hedging or other transaction which is designed to or which reasonably could be expected to lead to or result in a sale or disposition of the Holder’s Conversion Shares even if the Holder’s Conversion Shares would be disposed of by someone other than the Holder. Such prohibited hedging or other transactions would include, without limitation, any short sale or any purchase, sale or grant of any right (including, without limitation, any put or call option) with respect to any of the Holder’s Conversion Shares or with respect to any security that includes, relates to, or derives any significant part of its value from the Holder’s Conversion Shares. 1 Notwithstanding the foregoing, the Holder may transfer the Holder’s Conversion Shares (i) as a bona fide gift or gifts, provided that the donee or donees thereof agree to be bound in writing by the restrictions set forth herein; (ii) to any trust for the direct or indirect benefit of the Holder or the immediate family of the Holder, provided that the trustee of the trust agrees to be bound in writing by the restrictions set forth herein, and provided further that any such transfer shall not involve a disposition for value; (iii) to any corporation, partnership, limited liability company or other business entity, all of the beneficial ownership interests of which are held exclusively by the holder, domestic partner and/or one or more family members of the holder or the holder’s domestic partner in a transaction not involving a disposition for value; (iv) to one or more affiliates of the holder and distributions of securities to partners, members or shareholders of the holder; or (v) pursuant to a bona fide third party tender offer, merger, consolidation or other similar transaction made to all holders of common stock of the Company and involving a change of control; provided that in case of any transfer pursuant to clauses (i), (ii), (iii), and/or (iv), above, each transferee, donee or distributee shall sign and deliver a lock-up letter substantially in the form of this Lock-Up Agreement, and provided further that such transfer shall not involve a disposition for value and such transfer is not required to be reported in any public report or filing with the SEC during the Lock-Up Period. For purposes of this Lock-Up Agreement, “immediate family” shall mean any relationship by blood, marriage, domestic partnership or adoption, not more remote than first cousin. The Holder now has, and, except as contemplated by the immediately preceding sentence, for the duration of this Lock-Up Agreement will have, good and marketable title to the Conversion Shares, free and clear of all liens, encumbrances, and claims whatsoever. The Holder also agrees and consents to the entry of stop transfer instructions with the Company’s transfer agent, VStock Transfer, LLC, against the transfer of the Holder’s Conversion Shares except in compliance with the foregoing restrictions. Leak-Out Provisions Commencing upon the expiration or other termination of the Lock-Up Period, The Holder agrees, on behalf of itself and its affiliates that control, are controlled by, or are under common investment discretion with, the Holder with respect to any Conversion Shares, that the aggregate number of shares of Common Stock sold or otherwise disposed of by the Holder in any calendar week shall not exceed ten percent (10%) of the total number of Conversion Shares originally issued to the Holder. General The Holder hereby represents that the Holder has the power and authority to execute, deliver and perform this Lock-Up Agreement. The Holder understands and agrees that this Lock-Up Agreement is irrevocable and shall be binding upon the Holder’s heirs, legal representatives, successors, and assigns. This Lock-Up Agreement may be executed in two counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original but both of which shall be considered one and the same instrument. This Lock-Up Agreement will be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Nevada, without giving effect to any choice of law or conflicting provision or rule (whether of the State of Nevada, or any other jurisdiction) that would cause the laws of any jurisdiction other than the State of Nevada to be applied. In furtherance of the foregoing, the internal laws of the State of Nevada will control the interpretation and construction of this Lock-Up Agreement, even if under such jurisdiction’s choice of law or conflict of law analysis, the substantive law of some other jurisdiction would ordinarily apply. [Remainder of page intentionally left blank] 2 Very truly yours, Doron Kempel, Chief Executive Officer and Director Agreed to and Acknowledged: “Holder” Print name of Holder: _______________________ Signature:______________________________________ [if Holder is an entity]: Signatory name: __________________________ Signatory Title: __________________________ 3

text: EX-10.2 3 ipower_ex1002.htm WAIVER AND CONSENT, DATED NOVEMBER 16, 2026 Exhibit 10.2 LIMITED WAIVER AGREEMENT This Limited Waiver Agreement (the “ Agreement ”), dated as of November 16, 2026, is by and between iPower Inc., a Nevada corporation (the “ Company ”), and the holder identified on the signature page attached hereto (the “ Holder ”). R E C I T A L S A. Reference is hereby made to that certain Securities Purchase Agreement, dated as of December 22, 2025 (as amended, restated, supplemented and modified from time to time, the “ Securities Purchase Agreement ”), by and among the Company and the investors signatory thereto (the “ Buyers ”), pursuant to which, among other things, the Company issued to the Buyers certain Notes, which are convertible into shares of common stock, $0.001 par value per share, of the Company (the “ Common Stock ”). Capitalized terms used but not defined herein shall have the meanings set forth in the Securities Purchase Agreement. B. The Company desires to enter into a securities purchase agreement (the “ Subsequent Placement Agreement ”) with one or more investors that are not affiliates of any of the Buyers (the “ New Investors ”), in one or more offerings, pursuant to which, among other things, the Company would issue and sell to the New Investors up to $3,000,000 in aggregate purchase price of shares of Common Stock at a New Issuance Price per share of Common Stock not less than the “Minimum Price” (as defined in Nasdaq Listing Rule 5635(d)) in effect as of the date of execution of the Subsequent Placement Agreement (the “ Proposed Offerings ”). C. The Company desires that the Holder, in its capacity as a Required Holder, waive, in part, Section 4(o), Section 4(s), and Section 4(t) of the Securities Purchase Agreement, solely with respect to the Proposed Offerings, as necessary to permit the consummation of the transactions contemplated by the Subsequent Placement Agreement (the “ Limited Waivers ”). NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the foregoing premises and the mutual covenants hereinafter contained, the Company and the Holder agree as follows: A G R E E M E N T 1. Limited Waivers . Effective as of the Effective Date (as defined below), the Holder, in its capacity as a Required Holder, hereby grants the Limited Waivers. 2. Limitation of Waiver . The Limited Waivers set forth herein constitute a one-time waiver and are limited to the matters expressly waived herein and should not be construed as an indication that the Holder would be willing to agree to any future modifications to, consent to, or waiver of any of the terms of any other agreement, instrument or security or any modifications to, consents to, or waiver of any default that may exist or occur thereunder. 1 3. Ratifications . Except as otherwise expressly provided herein, each of the Transaction Documents is, and shall continue to be, in full force and effect and is hereby ratified and confirmed in all respects. 4. Fees and Expenses . The Company shall reimburse Kelley Drye & Warren, LLP (counsel to the Holder) in an aggregate non-accountable amount of $7,000 for costs and expenses incurred by it in connection with the drafting and negotiation of this Agreement (the “ Legal Fee Amount ”). Each party to this Agreement shall bear its own expenses in connection with the structuring, documentation, negotiation and closing of the transactions contemplated hereby, except as provided in the previous sentence and except that the Company shall be responsible for the payment of any placement agent’s fees, financial advisory fees, transfer agent fees and Depository Trust Company fees relating to or arising out of the transactions contemplated hereby. 5. Effective Date . This Agreement shall be deemed effective as of the date hereof upon the later of (x) the date on which this Agreement has been executed and delivered by each of the Company and the Holder and (ii) the date on which the Company has paid the Legal Fee Amount in full (the “ Effective Date ”). 6. Disclosure . On or before 9:00 a.m., New York City time, on the first (1st) Business Day after the date of this Agreement, the Company shall file a Current Report on Form 8-K describing any material non-public information the Company may have provided to the undersigned in relation to this Agreement or otherwise in the form required by the 1934 Act and attaching this Agreement as exhibits to such filing (the “ 8-K Filing ”). From and after the filing of the 8-K Filing with the SEC, the undersigned shall not be in possession of any material, nonpublic information received from the Company, any of its Subsidiaries or any of their respective officers, directors, employees, affiliates or agents. In addition, the Company acknowledges and agrees that any and all confidentiality or similar obligations under any agreement, whether written or oral, between the Company, any of its Subsidiaries or any of their respective officers, directors, affiliates, employees or agents on the one hand, and the undersigned or any of its affiliates on the other hand, has terminated as of the date hereof and is of no further force or effect. The Company shall not, and shall cause each of its Subsidiaries and its and each of their respective officers, directors, affiliates, employees and agents, not to, provide any undersigned with any material, non-public information regarding the Company or any of its Subsidiaries from and after the date hereof without the express prior written consent of the undersigned. To the extent that the Company, any of its Subsidiaries or any of their respective officers, directors, affiliates employees or agents delivers any material, non-public information to any undersigned without the undersigned’s consent, the Company hereby covenants and agrees that the undersigned shall not have any duty of confidentiality to the Company, any of its Subsidiaries or any of their respective officers, directors, affiliates, employees or agents with respect to, or a duty to the Company, any of its Subsidiaries or any of their respective officers, directors, affiliates, employees or agents not to trade on the basis of, such material, non-public information. The Company understands and confirms that the undersigned will rely on the foregoing representations in effecting transactions in securities of the Company. 7. Miscellaneous Provisions . Section 9 of the Securities Purchase Agreement is hereby incorporated by reference herein, mutatis mutandis . title: Perfect Moment Ltd.
text: EX-10.1 2 ex10-1.htm EX-10.1 Exhibit 10.1 EXECUTION VERSION THIRD AMENDMENT TO LOAN AGREEMENT THIS THIRD AMENDMENT TO LOAN AGREEMENT (this “ Amendment ”) is effective as of November 16, 2026 (the “ Amendment Effective Date ”), by and among PERFECT MOMENT LTD., a Delaware corporation (the “ Borrower ”), the Required Lenders (as defined in the Loan Agreement) signatory hereto and X3 HIGHER MOMENT FUND LLC, a Delaware limited liability company, in its capacity as administrative agent for the Lenders (in such capacity, the “ Administrative Agent ”). R E C I T A L S : WHEREAS, the Borrower, the Guarantors, the Lenders and the Administrative Agent entered into that certain Loan Agreement dated as of March 30, 2026 (as amended by that certain First Amendment to Loan Agreement effective as of August 20, 2026, as further amended by that certain Second Amendment and Limited Waiver to Loan Agreement effective as of October 9, 2026 (the “ Second Amendment ”), and as further amended, modified, supplemented or restated from time to time, the “ Loan Agreement ”). Capitalized terms used in this Amendment that are not otherwise defined in this Amendment shall have the respective meanings assigned to them in the Loan Agreement or, where so indicated, the Second Amendment. WHEREAS, the Borrower has advised the Administrative Agent of changes to its senior management and has requested that the definition of “Key Person” in the Loan Agreement be amended to identify Suzy Biszantz and Virginie Troudet as the Key Persons, and the Administrative Agent and the Required Lenders are willing to agree to such amendment on the terms and subject to the conditions set forth herein. WHEREAS, pursuant to Section 3 of the Second Amendment, the Administrative Agent and the Required Lenders waived, for the Waiver Period (as defined in the Second Amendment), certain restrictions on Revolving Credit Advances and certain Defaults and Events of Default arising from the Specified Key Person Event (as defined in the Second Amendment), and the parties hereto wish to confirm the treatment of the Specified Key Person Event in light of the amendments set forth herein. WHEREAS, the parties hereto desire to amend certain provisions of the Loan Agreement pursuant to the terms and conditions set forth herein. WHEREAS, the Borrower, the Administrative Agent and the Required Lenders constitute the parties required to amend the Loan Agreement pursuant to Section 9.04(b) thereof. 1 NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the Recitals and the mutual promises contained herein and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the Borrower, the Required Lenders and the Administrative Agent agree as follows: SECTION 1. Recitals . The Recitals are incorporated herein by reference and shall be deemed to be a part of this Amendment. SECTION 2. Amendments to Loan Agreement . Effective as of the Amendment Effective Date, the Loan Agreement is hereby amended as follows: (a) Section 1.01 of the Loan Agreement is hereby amended by amending and restating the definition of “Key Person” in its entirety as follows: “Key Person” means each of: (i) Suzy Biszantz and (ii) Virginie Troudet. (b) Section 1.01 of the Loan Agreement is hereby further amended by amending and restating the definition of “Key Person Event” in its entirety as follows: “Key Person Event” means if any Key Person resigns, is terminated of employment or otherwise ceases his or her usual role with the Borrower or any of its Subsidiaries, as determined by the Administrative Agent, in its sole and absolute discretion. (c) Section 1.01 of the Loan Agreement is hereby further amended by amending and restating the definition of “Key Person Cure Period” in its entirety as follows: “Key Person Cure Period” means a period of forty-five (45) days from the resignation, termination of employment or cessation of usual role of a Key Person. SECTION 3. Specified Key Person Event . The Administrative Agent (with the approval of the Required Lenders, as evidenced by their execution of this Amendment) hereby (a) approves Suzy Biszantz and Virginie Troudet as successors with similar industry experience, reputation and expertise for the former Key Persons, for purposes of Section 2.03(c)(ii)(1) and Section 7.01(p) of the Loan Agreement and Section 3(d) of the Second Amendment, and (b) agrees that, as of the Amendment Effective Date, the Specified Key Person Event has been remedied and no Default or Event of Default arising therefrom is continuing. Nothing in this Section 3 shall constitute a waiver of, or consent with respect to, any Key Person Event occurring after the Amendment Effective Date. SECTION 4. No Other Amendment . Except for the amendments set forth above in Section 2 and the approval set forth in Section 3 , the text of the Loan Agreement shall remain unchanged and in full force and effect. On and after the Amendment Effective Date, all references to the Loan Agreement shall hereafter mean the Loan Agreement as amended by this Amendment. This Amendment is not intended to effect, nor shall it be construed as, a novation. The Loan Agreement and this Amendment shall be construed together as a single agreement. Nothing herein contained shall waive, annul, vary or affect any provision, condition, covenant or agreement contained in the Loan Agreement, except as herein amended, nor affect nor impair any rights, powers or remedies under the Loan Agreement as hereby amended. The Borrower promises and agrees to perform all of the requirements, conditions, agreements and obligations under the terms of the Loan Agreement, as heretofore and hereby amended, with the Loan Agreement, as amended, being hereby ratified and affirmed. The Borrower hereby expressly agrees that the Loan Agreement, as amended, is in full force and effect. 2 SECTION 5. Conditions to Effectiveness . The effectiveness of this Amendment and the obligations of the Administrative Agent and Lenders hereunder are subject to the following conditions: (a) receipt by the Administrative Agent from each of the parties hereto of a duly executed counterpart of this Amendment signed by such party; and (b) the fact that the representations and warranties of the Borrower contained in Section 6 of this Amendment shall be true and correct in all material respects on and as of the date hereof. SECTION 6. Representations and Warranties . The Borrower hereby represents and warrants to the Administrative Agent and Lenders as follows: (a) After giving effect to this Amendment, no Default or Event of Default under the Loan Documents has occurred and is continuing on the date hereof. (b) The Borrower has the power and authority to enter into this Amendment and to do all acts and things as are required or contemplated hereunder to be done, observed and performed by the Borrower. (c) This Amendment has been duly authorized, validly executed and delivered by one or more authorized officers of the Borrower and constitutes the legal, valid and binding obligations of the Borrower enforceable against the Borrower in accordance with its terms, provided that such enforceability is subject to general principles of equity and to bankruptcy, insolvency and similar laws affecting the enforcement of creditors’ rights generally. (d) The execution and delivery of this Amendment and the performance by the Borrower hereunder does not and will not, as a condition to such execution, delivery and performance, require the consent or approval of any third party, including without limitation any regulatory authority or governmental authority or agency having jurisdiction over the Borrower, nor be in contravention of or in conflict with the organizational or operational documents of the Borrower, or the provision of any statute, or any judgment, order or indenture, instrument, agreement or undertaking, to which the Borrower is party or by which the assets or properties of the Borrower are or may become bound. (e) On the Amendment Effective Date, both immediately prior to, and immediately after giving effect to, this Amendment, all representations and warranties of the Borrower set forth in the Loan Documents (including, without limitation, the representations and warranties of the Borrower contained in Article V of the Loan Agreement) shall be true and correct in all material respects. SECTION 7. Counterparts; Governing Law . This Amendment may be executed in multiple counterparts, each of which shall be deemed to be an original and all of which, taken together, shall constitute one and the same agreement. This Amendment shall be construed in accordance with and governed by the laws of the State of New York. 3 SECTION 8. Amendment . This Amendment may not be amended or modified without the written consent of the Borrower, Administrative Agent and the Required Lenders. SECTION 9. Effective Date . This Amendment shall be effective as of the Amendment Effective Date. SECTION 10. Further Assurances . The Borrower agrees to promptly take such action, upon the request of the Administrative Agent, as is necessary to carry out the intent of this Amendment. SECTION 11. Severability . Any provision of this Amendment that is prohibited or unenforceable in any jurisdiction shall, as to such jurisdiction, be ineffective only to the extent of such prohibition or unenforceability without invalidating the remainder of such provision or the remaining provisions hereof or thereof or affecting the validity or enforceability of such provision in any other jurisdiction.
