text: EX-10.2 3 ex10-2.htm EX-10.2 Exhibit 10.2 EXECUTION COPY SENIOR ADVISORY AGREEMENT This Senior Advisory Agreement (this “Agreement” ) is made as of November 15, 2026 (the “Effective Date” ) by and between: (1) PERFECT MOMENT (USA), INC. , a Delaware corporation with offices at 244 5 th Ave Ste 1219, New York, NY 10001 , being the wholly-owned US operating subsidiary of Perfect Moment Ltd. (OTCQB: PMNT) (the “Company” ); and (2) JANE GOTTSCHALK , an individual residing at [***] (the “Senior Advisor” ), each a “Party” and together the “Parties”. BACKGROUND (A) The Company and its affiliates (together, the “Group”) design and sell luxury skiwear and lifestyle apparel. (B) The Company wishes to engage the Senior Advisor to provide brand and creative consulting services from November 15, 2026 through November 14, 2027, and the Senior Advisor has agreed to provide such services, on the terms of this Agreement. 1. Engagement and Services 1.1 The Company engages the Senior Advisor, and the Senior Advisor agrees, to provide the consulting services described in Schedule A (the “Services”) to the Group’s senior leadership. 1.2 The Senior Advisor shall perform the Services with due skill, care and diligence, and shall comply with all reasonable and lawful written directions of the Chief Executive Officer of Perfect Moment Ltd. (“CEO”) and applicable Group policies made available to the Senior Advisor. 1.3 The Senior Advisor’s direct point of contact shall be the CEO of Perfect Moment Ltd. or such other person as the Company may reasonably designate. 1.4 The Senior Advisor shall continue to engage in supportive and cooperative behavior through the transition from employee to a Senior Advisor for the Company. 2. Term and Six Month Review This Agreement commences on the Effective Date and continues until November 14, 2027 (the “Term” ), unless terminated earlier in accordance with Section 2, Section 9 or extended by mutual written agreement of the parties. On or about the date falling five (5) months after the Effective Date (the “Review Date” ), the CEO, the Chairman of the Board and the Senior Advisor shall meet and confer in good faith to re-evaluate the senior advisory arrangement, the scope of the Services and the Fees payable thereunder. At any time within 10 days following the Review Date, either party may elect to wind down this Agreement by giving written notice to the other party (a “Wind-Down Notice” ). Unless the parties agree otherwise in writing, termination pursuant to a Wind-Down Notice shall take effect on the date falling six ( 6) months after the Effective Date (the “Wind-Down Date” ), and upon such termination: (a) no further Fees or other compensation shall be payable by the Company to the Senior Advisor in respect of any period following the Wind-Down Date; (b) the Senior Advisor shall have no claim against the Company for loss of Fees, loss of anticipated earnings or any other compensation in respect of the unexpired portion of the Term; and (c) all surviving obligations expressly stated to continue beyond termination, including without limitation, the confidentiality obligations at Section 7 and the post-termination restrictions at Section 13, shall remain in full force and effect. If neither party delivers a Wind-Down Notice within the period specified in this clause, this Agreement shall continue on its existing terms for the remainder of the Term, subject to any amendments agreed in writing by the parties following the Review Date. Following the Review Date, the Company may, in its sole discretion but without any obligation to do so, offer to: (a) broaden the scope of the Senior Advisor’s Services and subject to 4.1 increase the Fees payable thereunder; or (b) offer the Senior Advisor a return to employment within the Group on such terms as the Company may determine. Any such offer shall be made in writing and shall not take effect unless accepted in writing by the Senior Advisor. Nothing in this clause shall create any expectation of, or entitlement to, an offer of expanded engagement or employment. 3. Time Commitment 3.1 The Senior Advisor shall devote time as reasonably requested by the CEO, but in no event more than two (2) business days per month, to the Services during the Term. 3.2 Subject to the foregoing, the Senior Advisor may determine the manner, time and place of performing the Services, and may provide services to third parties during the Term provided this does not create a conflict of interest, compete directly with or interfere with performance of the Services. 4. Fees 4.1 In consideration of the Services, the Company shall pay the Senior Advisor a total fee of US$141,000 for the Term of this Agreement (the “Fee”), payable in monthly amounts of US$10,500 for the first six (6) months of the Term and rising to US$13,000 for the remainder of the Term on the last day of the calendar month, subject to Six Month Review provisions in Section 2 above. The initial monthly billing period shall commence on the Effective Date of this Agreement and run for one (1) full calendar month. Each subsequent billing period shall run consecutively from the same day of each succeeding calendar month (the “Billing Date”). The Senior Advisor shall issue an invoice on each monthly Billing Date for the Services performed during the preceding billing period in arrears. The Company shall pay each valid and undisputed invoice within thirty (30) days from the Billing Date (Net 30).” In addition to the monthly Fees payable under this Agreement, the Company shall pay the Senior Advisor a one-time payment of US$50,000 (the “Commencement Payment” ) within 30 business days of the Effective Date. The Commencement Payment is not conditional on the performance of any Services and shall not be repayable in any circumstances. The Commencement Payment is made in full and final satisfaction of any claim the Senior Advisor may have to any equity-linked compensation from the Company or any Group Company during the Term. For the avoidance of doubt, save for any equity awards previously granted to the Senior Advisor and vested prior to the Effective Date. 4.2 The Fee is inclusive of all taxes. The Senior Advisor is solely responsible for all local income taxes, self-employment taxes and other taxes arising from payments under this Agreement. 5. Expenses; Product Allowance; Personal Items. 5.1 Expenses. The Company shall reimburse the Senior Advisor for reasonable, documented out-of-pocket travel and business expenses properly incurred in performing the Services, provided such expenses are approved in advance by the Company and are supported by receipts, in accordance with the Group’s expenses policy. 5.2 Product Allowance. In addition to the Fees payable under this Agreement, the Company shall make available to the Senior Advisor, over the course of the twelve (12) month term of this Agreement, an aggregate allowance of Perfect Moment branded products with a total retail value not exceeding £10,000 (the “Product Allowance” ), to be utilised by the Senior Advisor in her capacity as brand and creative consultant to the Company. The Product Allowance shall be drawn down by the Senior Advisor by way of written request to the CEO, specifying the products requested. The Company shall fulfil each such request subject to product availability, and no cash equivalent or carry-over of any unused portion of the Product Allowance shall be payable at the end of the term or on earlier termination of this Agreement, howsoever arising. For the avoidance of doubt, the retail value of products provided pursuant to this clause shall be calculated by reference to the recommended retail price of the relevant products at the time of each request. The Product Allowance is provided for the Senior Advisor’s personal use and for use in connection with her brand activities, and the Senior Advisor shall not resell or transfer the products for commercial gain. The parties acknowledge that the provision of products pursuant to this clause may give rise to a taxable benefit, and the Senior Advisor shall be solely responsible for any income tax or other tax liability arising in connection with the receipt of products under this Agreement. 5.3 Personal Items. The parties acknowledge that certain personal artwork and furniture belonging to the Senior Advisor (the “Personal Items” ) are currently located at the Company’s premises. The Personal Items are listed at Schedule B . The Company shall pay the Senior Advisor a monthly fee of US$975 per calendar month (or pro rata for any part month) from the Effective Date until the date on which the Personal Items are removed from the Company’s premises in accordance with this clause (the “Removal Date” ), in consideration of the Personal Items remaining on the Company’s premises during that period. Such payments shall be made on or about the 28th day of each month alongside the Senior Advisor’s other payments under this Agreement. The Senior Advisor shall procure the removal of all Personal Items from the Company’s premises no later than 31 December 2026 (the “Removal Deadline” ). The Senior Advisor shall give the Company not less than 5 business days’ prior written notice of the intended removal date, and removal shall take place at a time reasonably convenient to the Company. The Company shall bear the reasonable costs of professionally packing and transporting the Personal Items, subject to the following conditions: (a) the Company’s obligation to meet removal costs is limited to transportation to a single destination within the United Kingdom ; the Company shall have no obligation to meet any costs of transportation outside the United Kingdom, and any such costs shall be borne solely by the Senior Advisor; and (b) the Company shall appoint a reputable packing and removal contractor. The Senior Advisor shall cooperate reasonably with the Company and the appointed contractor to facilitate safe packing and removal of the Personal Items. Risk in the Personal Items shall remain with the Senior Advisor at all times. The Company shall use reasonable care in handling the Personal Items prior to removal and shall maintain in force adequate contents insurance in respect of the Company’s premises until the Removal Date, but the Company shall not be liable for any loss of or damage to the Personal Items save to the extent caused by the Company’s own negligence or wilful default. If the Senior Advisor fails to procure removal of all Personal Items by the Removal Deadline: (a) the monthly fee under 5.3 shall cease to be payable with effect from 31 December 2026 and (b) the Company may, upon giving not less than 10 business days’ written notice to the Senior Advisor, arrange for the storage or removal of any remaining Personal Items at the Senior Advisor’s cost and risk, and shall have no further liability in connection with such items beyond taking reasonable steps to preserve them pending the Senior Advisor’s collection. 6. Independent Contractor The Senior Advisor is an independent contractor. Nothing in this Agreement creates an employment, agency, partnership or joint-venture relationship between the Parties. The Senior Advisor is not entitled to participate in any employee benefit plan of the Group and shall not hold herself out as having authority to bind the Group except as expressly authorized in writing. The Senior Advisor may refer to herself as Co-Founder of the modern Perfect Moment brand and Brand and Creative Senior Adviser to Perfect Moment. 7. Confidentiality; Securities Law Compliance 7.1 The Senior Advisor shall keep confidential and use solely for the purpose of performing the Services, all non-public information of or relating to the Group, its business, finances, products, suppliers, customers, personnel and plans (“Confidential Information”), during and after the Term. Confidential Information excludes information that is or becomes public other than through breach of this Agreement, or that the Senior Advisor is required to disclose by law. 7.2 The Senior Advisor acknowledges that Perfect Moment Ltd. is a company listed on the OTC QB Venture Market and that in performing the Services the Senior Advisor will receive material non-public information. The Senior Advisor shall comply with all applicable securities laws and with the Group’s insider trading policy, including refraining from dealing in the securities of Perfect Moment Ltd. while in possession of material non-public information and from communicating such information to any person who may deal in such securities. 8. Intellectual Property To the extent any of the Senior Advisor’s Services result in intellectual property (logos, names or designs) that are protectable by either trademark or design rights, it shall be owned by the Company as such; to the extent it does not, the Senior Advisor hereby assigns to the Company all right, title and interest in and to such intellectual property, and shall execute such documents as the Company reasonably requests to give effect to this Section. 9. Termination 9.1 The Senior Advisor may terminate this Agreement on thirty (30) days’ prior written notice; provided, however, that the Company shall have no further obligation to pay Fees upon termination by the Senior Advisor . Both parties are subject to the Six Month Review provisions set forth in Section 2 above. 9.2 The Company may terminate this Agreement with immediate effect by written notice if the Senior Advisor commits a material breach of this Agreement which (if capable of remedy) is not remedied within fourteen (14) days of notice. Save as provided in this Section 9.2, Section 2 and Section 10, the Company may not terminate this Agreement prior to the Wind-Down. 9.3 On expiration, termination or on the Wind-Down Date, whichever is earliest, the Company shall pay the Fee pro-rated to the date of termination together with properly incurred expenses, and the Senior Advisor shall return or destroy all Confidential Information and Group property. Sections 6, 7, 8, 9.3, 11, 12 and 13 survive termination 10. Cross-Default 10.1 The Senior Advisor has entered into a settlement agreement with the Company’s affiliate, Perfect Moment UK Limited (“PM UK”) dated November 15, 2026 (the “Settlement Agreement” ), pursuant to which the Senior Advisor’s employment with PM UK was terminated. The Senior Advisor’s obligations under the Settlement Agreement are material to the Company’s decision to enter into this Agreement. 10.2 Any material breach by the Senior Advisor of any term of the Settlement Agreement which (if capable of remedy) is not remedied within fourteen (14) days of notice shall constitute a material breach of this Agreement. For the avoidance of doubt, this includes but is not limited to any breach of the Senior Advisor’s obligations relating to confidentiality, non-disparagement, return of property, cooperation, restrictive covenants, or any warranty or representation given by the Senior Advisor under the Settlement Agreement. 10.3 In the event of a material breach of the Settlement Agreement by the Senior Advisor (as defined in Section 10.2), the Company shall be entitled, without prejudice to any other rights or remedies available to it at law or under this Agreement, to terminate this Agreement with immediate effect by written notice to the Senior Advisor, without any liability to pay further Fees or other compensation in respect of any period following the date of such termination. 10.4 The Company’s right to terminate under Section 10.3 shall not be affected by any delay in exercising that right, nor shall any prior waiver of a breach of the Settlement Agreement constitute a waiver of any subsequent breach or of the Company’s rights under this clause. 10.5 Where the Company exercises its right to terminate this Agreement pursuant to this clause, the provisions of this Agreement that are expressed to survive termination — including without limitation the confidentiality obligations at Section 7, the non-disparagement obligations at Section 11, and the post-termination restrictions at Section 13 — shall remain in full force and effect. 11. Non-Disparagement Each party agrees and covenants that it will not, at any time during the term of this Agreement or thereafter, directly or indirectly make, publish, post, broadcast, or communicate to any person or entity, or in any public or private forum (including without limitation on any social media platform, podcast, interview, blog, press release, or in any communication with media or press), any remarks, comments, or statements that are defamatory, disparaging, false, misleading, or otherwise harmful to the reputation or business interests of the other party. This obligation extends to the Company, any member of the Group, and the Senior Advisor, and each of their respective businesses, employees, officers, directors, shareholders, customers, suppliers, investors, and other associated third parties. Neither party shall, directly or indirectly, encourage, induce, or assist any third party to make any statement that would be prohibited by this Section if made by that party directly. This Section does not restrict either party from: (i) exercising any protected right that cannot be waived by agreement; (ii) complying with any applicable law, regulation, or valid order of a court of competent jurisdiction or authorized government agency, provided that such compliance does not exceed what is strictly required; or (iii) making truthful statements in any legal or regulatory proceeding in which that party is required to participate. Each party shall provide the other with written notice of any such order or requirement within forty-eight (48) hours of receipt. Each party acknowledges that a breach of this Section would cause irreparable harm to the other party for which monetary damages would be an inadequate remedy, and that the non-breaching party shall be entitled to seek injunctive or other equitable relief without the necessity of proving actual damages or posting any bond or other security, in addition to all other remedies available at law or in equity. 12. General 12.1 Entire Agreement. This Agreement (including its Schedules) constitutes the entire agreement between the Parties in relation to its subject matter and supersedes all prior discussions and correspondence. 12.2 Amendments; Waiver. Any amendment or waiver must be in writing and signed by both Parties. 12.3 Assignment. Neither Party may assign this Agreement without the prior written consent of the other, save that the Company may assign to any member of the Group. 12.4 Notices. Notices shall be in writing and delivered by hand, courier or email to the addresses set out above (or as notified in writing), and shall be deemed given on delivery (or, if by email, on transmission absent a bounce-back). 12.5 Governing Law; Jurisdiction. This Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of Delaware, without regard to its conflict-of-laws rules. The Parties submit to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in the State of Delaware. 12.6 Counterparts. This Agreement may be executed in counterparts (including by electronic signature), each of which is an original and which together constitute one agreement. 13. Post-Term Restrictions 13.1 Definitions. For purposes of this Section: “Restricted Period” means the period commencing on the Effective Date and, at the written election of the Company, ending no more than nine (9) months after the expiration or earlier termination of this Agreement; provided, however, that if the Company elects in writing to have the Restricted Period continue beyond the expiration or earlier termination of this Agreement, the Company shall continue to pay the monthly Fees specified in Section 4 above at the same rate as was in effect on the date of expiration or termination (either US$10,500 or US$13,000) for the duration of the continuation of such Restricted Period. The Company shall provide thirty (30) days written notice in order to terminate the post-term Restricted Period. The Restricted Period shall end automatically if the Company fails to pay a monthly amount more than ten (10) days after it was otherwise due to be paid and the Company has failed to cure within three (3) days of written notice of non-payment. If no written election is provided to extend the Restricted Period beyond expiration or termination of this Agreement, the Restricted Period shall end concurrently with the expiration of termination of this Agreement. “Competing Business” means any person or entity engaged in the design, development, marketing or sale of luxury skiwear products or alpine inspired products in competition with the Group, including the launch of a luxury skiwear line by a business not previously active in skiwear. The Senior Advisor shall not be in breach of Section 13.2 by providing services to a business in respect of product categories other than skiwear, provided that she has no involvement in that business’s skiwear activities. For the avoidance of doubt, “alpine inspired products” means ski and après-ski apparel. “Restricted Customer” means any person or entity that was a wholesale account, or prospective wholesale account of the Group at any time during the twelve (12) months preceding the date of termination, and with whom the Senior Advisor had material contact or about whom the Senior Advisor received Confidential Information in the course of her engagement. “Restricted Employee” means any person employed or engaged by the Group at the level of manager or above at any time during the six (6) months preceding the date of termination. 13.2 Non-Compete. During the Restricted Period, the Senior Advisor shall not, directly or indirectly, whether as an employee, director, officer, consultant, partner, investor, or otherwise, carry on, be engaged in or provide services in respect of any Competing Business. Nothing in this Section prohibits the Senior Advisor from holding a passive investment of less than two percent (2%) of the outstanding securities of any publicly traded company. 13.3 Non-Solicitation of Customers. During the Restricted Period, the Senior Advisor shall not, directly or indirectly, solicit, induce, or attempt to solicit or induce any Restricted Customer to reduce, terminate, or divert any business with the Group, or to direct any business to any Competing Business. 13.4 Non-Solicitation of Employees. During the Restricted Period, the Senior Advisor shall not, directly or indirectly, solicit, recruit, hire, or attempt to solicit, recruit, or hire any Restricted Employee away from the Group, or induce or attempt to induce any Restricted Employee to terminate their relationship with the Group. 13.5 No Proactive Account Contact. During the Term, the Senior Advisor shall not initiate any proactive contact with wholesale accounts that are existing clients of the Group or that the Company has been in contact with during the last 24 months without the prior written consent of the CEO. For the avoidance of doubt, this restriction applies to contact through any medium, including email, telephone, social media, or in person, but does not apply to social or personal contact that does not concern a Competing Business or the business of the Group. 13.6 Reasonableness. The Senior Advisor acknowledges that the restrictions in this Section are reasonable and necessary to protect the legitimate business interests of the Group, including its confidential information, customer relationships, and workforce stability, and that the compensation paid under this Agreement constitutes adequate consideration for these restrictions. 13.7 Enforceability; Reformation. If any restriction in this Section is held unenforceable by a court of competent jurisdiction, the Parties authorize the court to modify the restriction to the minimum extent necessary to make it enforceable, and the remaining restrictions shall continue in full force. 13.8 Injunctive Relief. The Senior Advisor acknowledges that a breach of this Section would cause irreparable harm to the Group for which monetary damages would be an inadequate remedy, and that the Company shall be entitled to seek injunctive or other equitable relief without the necessity of proving actual damages or posting any bond or other security, in addition to all other remedies available at law or in equity. [Signature page follows] IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the Parties have executed this Agreement as of the Effective Date. PERFECT MOMENT (USA), INC. text: EX-10.4 5 ex10-4.htm EX-10.4 Exhibit 10.4 Execution Copy Employment Contract Between Perfect Moment International AG C/O KD ZUG Treuhand AG Untermulli 7, 6302 Zug Switzerland (hereinafter referred to as the “Employer”) And Virginie Alexandra Troudet [***] (hereinafter referred to as the “Employee”) This employment contract is subject to the provision that a work permit is granted by the relevant authorities or that the employee already has a valid work permit. The following employment contract is concluded: 1. Position and Department The Employee is promoted to Chief Financial Officer to lead the finance department of the Employer reporting to the to the Chief Executive Officer and with direct access to the Audit Committee of the Board of Directors 2. Start Date The employment relationship began on 17 th February 2025. The promotion took effect on November 16, 2026 with a retroactive effect on payment of salary as of September 1, 2026. The pre-tax payment amount for September 2026 shall be CHF 4,875. This contract is concluded for an indefinite period. Degree of employment: 100% 3. Probation Period The probation period has been completed satisfactorily, and no new probation period is required. 4. Place of Work The Employee’s primary place of work is Switzerland. The Employer reserves the right to change the place of work within Switzerland, with prior notice to the Employee. 5. Working Hours The Employee’s regular working hours are 40 hours per week, from Monday to Friday. The regular daily working hours in general last from 09:00–17:00. Overtime may be required as per operational needs and will be compensated according to Swiss law or company policy. 6. Salary The Employee’s gross monthly salary is CHF 245,000, payable in 12 installments per year. Payment is made on or before the 25th of each month into an account designated by the Employee. Additional bonuses or allowances: ● Bonus: For each calendar year of employment, you shall be eligible to receive an annual bonus (the “Annual Bonus”). Your target Annual Bonus is thirty percent (30%) of the your base salary. However, the decision to provide any Annual Bonus and the amount and terms of any Annual Bonus shall be in the sole and absolute discretion of the Board and the Compensation Committee of the Board but shall be based achieving or exceeding annual goals, which are likely to include the Company’s approved budget for annual sales and EBITDA, but which will be set prior to the start of each fiscal budget year (the “Compensation Committee”). The Annual Bonus shall be prorated based on the Company’s results at the end of each fiscal year which is not a full fiscal year for the Company (April 1 – March 31). By way of example, your first Annual Bonus shall be prorated for the period from November 16, 2026 – March 31, 2027; ● Equity: A one-time grant equal to 750,000 Restricted Stock Units upon your promotion start date with annual vesting over four years. Thereafter, you shall be eligible to be included in the annual 2021 Equity Incentive plan grant program in amounts and terms awarded to similarly situated executive employees. All equity grants to the Employee shall vest upon a change of control of the company, in accordance with the terms of the 2021 Equity Incentive Plan, or upon a termination of the Employee’s employment without cause or for good reason within 12 months of September 1. Legally stipulated social security contributions, all compulsory occupational insurance contributions, and any other deductions as legally prescribed or agreed with the Employee will be deducted at source from the salary and/or applicable Bonus or Equity Award. 7. Vacation Entitlement The Employee is entitled to 25 working days of paid vacation per year, in accordance with Swiss law. Vacation must be approved in advance by the Employer. 8. Social Benefits and Insurance • Pension Fund (2nd Pillar): The Employee will be enrolled in the Employer’s pension scheme as required by Swiss law (BVG). Contributions will be shared between Employer and Employee as per legal requirements. ● Accident Insurance: The Employer provides occupational and non-occupational accident insurance as mandated by Swiss law. ● Health Insurance: The Employee is responsible for obtaining mandatory Swiss health insurance (KVG). 9. Confidentiality The Employee undertakes to maintain strict confidentiality regarding all business and trade secrets of the Employer, both during and after the employment relationship. Inventions and designs created by the Employee alone or in collaboration with others while carrying out his/her professional activities are considered to have been fully ceded to the Employer. The Employee cedes in full to the Employer all intellectual property right, including, but not limited to, copyrights, trademarks, design rights, trade secrets and/or patent rights, unlimited in time or location, to the results of work, including computer programs, commenced or fully developed alone or in collaboration with others while carrying out his/her professional duties. This assignment of rights applies to all economic rights (including amendments rights), and to all current and future utilization forms and field of application pertaining to the results of work in question. Compensation for the transfer of such rights is included in the agreed salary. 10. Directors and Officers Liability Insurance. (a) Coverage During Employment . Throughout the employment term, the Employer or its affiliate shall obtain and maintain Directors and Officers liability insurance ( “D&O Insurance” ) providing coverage for the Employee on terms and in amounts no less favorable than those provided to any other senior officer or director of the Employer. (b) Personal Tail Policy Upon Departure . Upon the termination of the Employee’s employment for any reason — including resignation, termination with or without cause, expiration of the employment term, death, or disability — the Employer shall, at its sole expense, purchase and maintain a personal Directors and Officers liability tail policy (also known as an extended reporting period endorsement) in favor of the Employee (the “Tail Policy” ), providing the following minimum terms: (i) Coverage Period: Six (6) years from the date of the Employee’s last day of employment (the “Departure Date” ); (ii) Scope of Coverage: Coverage for claims first made during the six (6)-year tail period arising out of or relating to any actual or alleged act, error, omission, misstatement, misleading statement, neglect, or breach of duty by the Employee in the Employee’s capacity as Chief Financial Officer, director, or officer of the Employer or any subsidiary or affiliate of the Employer, occurring prior to or on the Departure Date; (iii) Coverage Amount: Coverage limits no less than those in effect under the Employer’s D&O Insurance policy immediately prior to the Departure Date; and (iv) Insurer: The Tail Policy shall be placed with an insurer of recognized financial standing reasonably acceptable to the Employee and shall be placed on terms no less favorable to the Employee than the terms of the Employer’s then-current D&O Insurance policy. (c) Timing of Tail Policy Purchase . The Employer, or its ultimate parent company, Perfect Moment Ltd., shall purchase the Tail Policy no later than thirty (30) days following the Departure Date. The cost of the Tail Policy shall be borne entirely by the Employer and shall not be deducted from or offset against any severance or other amounts payable to the Employee. 11. Indemnification In the event that you are made a party or threatened to be made a party to any action, suit or proceeding, whether civil, criminal, administrative or investigative (a “Proceeding”), other than any Proceeding initiated by you or the Company related to any contest or dispute between you and the Company or any of its affiliates with respect to this Agreement or your employment hereunder, by reason of the fact that you are or were a director or officer of the Company, or any affiliate of the Company, or is or was serving at the request of the Company as a director, officer, member, employee or agent of another corporation or a partnership, joint venture, trust or other enterprise, the Executive shall be indemnified and held harmless by the Company to the extent applicable to similarly situated officers or directors of the Company, but no more than the maximum extent permitted under applicable law and the Company’s bylaws, from and against any liabilities, costs, claims and expenses, including all costs and expenses incurred in defense of any Proceeding (including attorneys’ fees). 12. Non-Compete Clause For a period of 6 months after the termination of this contract, the Employee agrees not to engage in any activity that directly competes with the Employer’s business of luxury skiwear/outerwear within Switzerland and the United Kingdom, unless otherwise agreed in writing. 13. Termination and Severance After the probation period, the notice period for termination for either party is two weeks. Termination must be in writing. If the Employee’s employment is terminated by the Employer without cause, or by the employee for good reason, the Employee shall be entitled to receive Employee’s continued base salary for six (6) months following the termination date payable in equal installments in accordance with the Company’s normal payroll practices, in addition to the standard notice period. 14. Applicable Law and Jurisdiction This contract is governed by Swiss law, in particular the Swiss Code of Obligations (OR). Any disputes arising from this contract shall be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of Zug. 15. Amendments Any amendments or additions to this contract must be made in writing and signed by both parties. 16. Signatures This contract is drawn up in duplicate. Each party acknowledges receipt of one copy. Zug, November 16, 2026 Employer /s/ Suzy Biszantz Suzy Biszantz Chief Executive Officer Employee /s/ Virginie Alexandra Troudet Virginie Alexandra Troudet Perfect Moment Ltd, with respect to the obligations in Section 10: Perfect Moment Ltd. /s/ Suzy Biszantz Suzy Biszantz Chief Executive Officer

text: EX-10.1 2 tm2629917d1_ex10-1.htm EXHIBIT 10.1 Exhibit 10.1 THIS PROMISSORY NOTE (THIS “NOTE”) HAS NOT BEEN REGISTERED UNDER THE SECURITIES ACT OF 1933, AS AMENDED (THE “SECURITIES ACT”). THIS NOTE HAS BEEN ACQUIRED FOR INVESTMENT ONLY AND MAY NOT BE SOLD, TRANSFERRED OR ASSIGNED IN THE ABSENCE OF REGISTRATION OF THE RESALE THEREOF UNDER THE SECURITIES ACT OR AN OPINION OF COUNSEL REASONABLY SATISFACTORY IN FORM, SCOPE AND SUBSTANCE TO THE COMPANY THAT SUCH REGISTRATION IS NOT REQUIRED. PROMISSORY NOTE Principal Amount: Up to US$1,000,000 Dated as of November 10, 2026 Spark I Acquisition Corporation, a Cayman Islands exempted company and blank check company (the “ Maker ”), promises to pay to the order of SLG SPAC Fund LLC, a Delaware limited liability company, or its registered assigns or successors in interest (the “ Payee ”), the entire unpaid Principal Amount (as defined below) of up to One Million U.S. Dollars (US$1,000,000) in lawful money of the United States of America, on the terms and conditions described below. All payments on this Note shall be made by check or wire transfer of immediately available funds or as otherwise determined by the Maker to such account as the Payee may from time to time designate by written notice in accordance with the provisions of this Note. 1. Principal . The entire unpaid principal balance of this Note shall be due and payable on the Maturity Date unless earlier repaid or unless accelerated upon the occurrence of an Event of Default (as defined below). “ Maturity Date ” means the earlier of the (i) consummation of the Maker’s initial merger, share capital exchange, asset acquisition, share purchase, reorganization or similar business combination with one or more businesses or entities (a “ Business Combination ”) and (ii) the last day the Maker has to complete a Business Combination pursuant to the Maker’s Amended and Restated Memorandum and Articles of Association, as then in effect. The Payee understands that if a Business Combination is not consummated, this Note will be repaid solely to the extent that the Maker has funds available to it outside of its trust account established in connection with its initial public offering of its securities (the “ Trust Account ”). The Principal Amount may be prepaid at any time. Under no circumstances shall any individual, including, but not limited to, any officer, director, employee or shareholder of the Maker, be obligated personally for any obligations or liabilities of the Maker under this Note. 2. Interest . No interest shall accrue on the unpaid Principal Amount of this Note. 3. Advances; Drawdown Requests . (a) Advances . If the Extension Amendment Proposal (as defined in the Proxy Statement) is approved and adopted, beginning on October 1, 2026, and on the eleventh (11th) day of each subsequent month until the Maturity Date (or if such day is not a business day, on the business day immediately preceding such day), the Payee shall advance (each, an “ Advance ”) directly to the Trust Account an amount equal to US$0.015 for each outstanding Class A ordinary share, par value US$0.0001 per share, of the Maker. No fees, payments or other amounts shall be due to Payee in connection with, or as a result of, any Advances by Payee. (b) Drawdown Requests . Maker and Payee agree that Maker may request, from time to time, up to One Million U.S. Dollars (US$1,000,000) minus the maximum aggregate amount of Advances payable under this Note, in Drawdown Requests (as defined below) under this Note to be used for working capital expenditures, including expenses incurred in connection with a potential Business Combination. Principal of this Note may be drawn down from time to time prior to the Maturity Date upon written request from Maker to Payee (each, a “ Drawdown Request ” and, the sum of all Advances and Drawdown Requests, the “ Principal Amount ”). Each Drawdown Request must state the amount to be drawn down and must not be an amount less than Ten Thousand U.S. Dollars (US$10,000), unless agreed upon in writing by Maker and Payee. Payee shall fund each Drawdown Request no later than three (3) business days after receipt of a Drawdown Request. No fees, payments or other amounts shall be due to Payee in connection with, or as a result of, any Drawdown Request by Maker. (c) Principal Amount . The Principal Amount outstanding under this Note at any time may not exceed One Million U.S. Dollars (US$1,000,000). (d) Register . The Maker shall maintain a register reflecting each Advance and Drawdown Request and any prepayment of all or a portion of the Principal Amount outstanding under this Note for purposes of recording the aggregate unpaid Principal Amoun of this Note outstanding at any time. 4. Application of Payments . All payments shall be applied first to payment in full of any costs incurred in the collection of any sum due under this Note, including (without limitation) reasonable attorney’s fees, then to the payment in full of any late charges and finally to the reduction of the unpaid Principal Amount of this Note. 5. Events of Default . The following shall constitute an event of default (“ Event of Default ”): (a) Failure to Make Required Payments . Failure by the Maker to pay the unpaid Principal Amount due pursuant to this Note within five (5) business days following the Maturity Date. (b) Voluntary Bankruptcy , Etc . The commencement by the Maker of a voluntary case under any applicable bankruptcy, insolvency, reorganization, rehabilitation or other similar law, or the consent by it to the appointment of or taking possession by a receiver, liquidator, assignee, trustee, custodian, sequestrator (or other similar official) of the Maker or for any substantial part of its property, or the making by it of any assignment for the benefit of creditors, or the failure of the Maker generally to pay its debts as such debts become due, or the taking of corporate action by the Maker in furtherance of any of the foregoing. (c) Involuntary Bankruptcy , Etc . The entry of a decree or order for relief by a court having jurisdiction in the premises in respect of the Maker in an involuntary case under any applicable bankruptcy, insolvency or other similar law, or appointing a receiver, liquidator, assignee, custodian, trustee, sequestrator (or similar official) of the Maker or for any substantial part of its property, or ordering the winding-up or liquidation of its affairs, and the continuance of any such decree or order unstayed and in effect for a period of 60 consecutive days. 6. Remedies . (a) Upon the occurrence of an Event of Default specified in Section 5(a) hereof, the Payee may, by written notice to the Maker, declare this Note to be due immediately and payable, whereupon the unpaid Principal Amount of this Note, and all other amounts payable hereunder, shall become immediately due and payable without presentment, demand, protest or other notice of any kind, all of which are hereby expressly waived, anything contained in this Note or in the documents evidencing the same to the contrary notwithstanding. (b) Upon the occurrence of an Event of Default specified in Section 5(b) or Section 5(c), the unpaid Principal Amount, and all other sums payable with regard to this Note, shall automatically and immediately become due and payable, in all cases without any action on the part of the Payee. 7. Waivers . The Maker and all endorsers and guarantors of, and sureties for, this Note waive presentment for payment, demand, notice of dishonor, protest, and notice of protest with regard to this Note, all errors, defects and imperfections in any proceedings instituted by the Payee under the terms of this Note, and all benefits that might accrue to the Maker by virtue of any present or future laws exempting any property, real or personal, or any part of the proceeds arising from any sale of any such property, from attachment, levy or sale under execution, or providing for any stay of execution, exemption from civil process, or extension of time for payment; and the Maker agrees that any real estate that may be levied upon pursuant to a judgment obtained by virtue hereof, or any writ of execution issued hereon, may be sold upon any such writ in whole or in part in any order desired by the Payee. 8. Unconditional Liability . The Maker hereby waives all notices in connection with the delivery, acceptance, performance, default, or enforcement of the payment of this Note, and agrees that its liability shall be unconditional, without regard to the liability of any other party, and shall not be affected in any manner by any indulgence, extension of time, renewal, waiver or modification granted or consented to by the Payee, and consents to any and all extensions of time, renewals, waivers, or modifications that may be granted by the Payee with respect to the payment or other provisions of this Note, and agrees that additional makers, endorsers, guarantors, or sureties may become parties to this Note without notice to the Maker or affecting the Maker’s liability hereunder. 9. Notices . All notices, statements or other documents which are required or contemplated by this Note shall be made in writing and delivered: (i) personally or sent by first class registered or certified mail, overnight courier service or facsimile or electronic transmission to the address designated in writing, (ii) by facsimile to the number most recently provided to such party or such other address or fax number as may be designated in writing by such party or (iii) by electronic mail, to the electronic mail address most recently provided to such party or such other electronic mail address as may be designated in writing by such party. Any notice or other communication so transmitted shall be deemed to have been given on the day of delivery, if delivered personally, on the business day following receipt of written confirmation, if sent by facsimile or electronic transmission, one (1) business day after delivery to an overnight courier service or five (5) days after mailing if sent by mail. 10. Construction . THIS NOTE SHALL BE CONSTRUED AND ENFORCED IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE LAWS OF THE STATE OF NEW YORK, WITHOUT REGARD TO CONFLICT OF LAW PROVISIONS THEREOF. 11. Severability . Any provision contained in this Note that is prohibited or unenforceable in any jurisdiction shall, as to such jurisdiction, be ineffective to the extent of such prohibition or unenforceability without invalidating the remaining provisions hereof, and any such prohibition or unenforceability in any jurisdiction shall not invalidate or render unenforceable such provision in any other jurisdiction. 12. Trust Waiver . Notwithstanding anything in this Note to the contrary, the Payee waives any and all right, title, interest or claim of any kind (“ Claim ”) in or to any distribution of or from, the Trust Account, and agrees not to seek recourse, reimbursement, payment or satisfaction for any Claim against the Trust Account for any reason whatsoever. 13. Amendment; Waiver . Any amendment to this Note or waiver of any provision of this Note may be made with, and only with, the written consent of the Maker and the Payee. 14. Assignment . No assignment or transfer of this Note or any rights or obligations hereunder may be made by any party to this Note (by operation of law or otherwise) without the prior written consent of the other party to this Note and any attempted assignment without the required consent shall be void. [Remainder of Page Intentionally Left Blank] IN WITNESS WHEREOF , the Maker, intending to be legally bound hereby, has caused this Note to be duly executed by the undersigned as of the day and year first above written. Spark I Acquisition Corporation a Cayman Islands exempted company By: /s/ James Rhee Name: James Rhee Title: Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Accepted and Agreed: SLG SPAC Fund LLC By: SparkLabs Group Management, LLC, its Managing Member By: /s/ Bernard Moon Name: Bernard Moon Title: Managing Member [Signature Page to Promissory Note]

text: EX-10.2 3 d109046dex102.htm EX-10.2 EX-10.2 Exhibit 10.2 Execution Version November 10, 2026 Re: Acknowledgment Regarding GM Letters of Credit and Amendment to Limited Liability Company Agreement Ladies and Gentlemen: This letter agreement (this “ Agreement ”), dated as of November 10, 2026 (the “ Effective Date ”), is entered into by and among Lithium Nevada Ventures LLC, a Delaware limited liability company (the “ Company ”), General Motors Holdings LLC, a Delaware limited liability company (“ GM ”), and LAC US Corp., a Nevada corporation (“ LAC ” and, collectively with the Company and GM, the “ Parties ”). Reference is hereby made to that certain Second Amended and Restated Limited Liability Company Agreement of Lithium Nevada Ventures LLC, dated as of January 30, 2026 (the “ LLCA ”). Capitalized terms used but not otherwise defined in this Agreement have the meanings assigned to them in the LLCA. The Parties hereby agree as follows: 1. GM Letters of Credit. GM acknowledges and agrees that the GM Letters of Credit may be drawn upon in accordance with the terms of the DOE Loan (as amended). In respect of any amount so drawn and paid, neither GM nor its Affiliates shall be required to reinstate such amount or provide replacement funding or credit support for any DOE Reserve Account. GM’s rights under Section 9.1(a)(i) of the LLCA, including the existing conditions and priorities applicable thereto, are preserved. In connection with any draw under any GM Letter of Credit, the Company shall cause the Subsidiary Borrower to provide GM with copies of any confirmations, consents and certificates provided to or received from DOE, the Collateral Agent (as defined in the DOE Loan) and the applicable issuer of such GM Letter of Credit required to be obtained by the Company or the Subsidiary Borrower in connection with such draw. This Agreement does not amend any GM Letter of Credit or Financing Document (as defined in the DOE Loan). 2. Ownership Thresholds. For purposes of this Agreement, (i) “ Protection Date ” means the second (2 nd ) anniversary of the Project Completion Date (as defined in the DOE Loan), and (ii) “ Protection Period ” means the period beginning with the Effective Date and ending on the earlier of (a) the date on which GM or its Affiliates first Transfers any Units (other than a Transfer to an Affiliate), and (b) the later of (x) the Protection Date, and (y) solely to the extent a Top-Up Notice has been provided pursuant to paragraph 6 prior to the Protection Date, the date on which GM has funded its Capital Contribution and the Company has issued the corresponding Units pursuant to paragraph 6(iii) (or such earlier date on which the Top-Up Notice is withdrawn or otherwise lapses or GM fails to fund such Capital Contribution when due pursuant to paragraph 6(iii)). The Company shall cause the Subsidiary Borrower to notify GM and LAC in writing within five (5) Business Days after the Project Completion Date, together with reasonable supporting data and evidence of achievement thereof. During the Protection Period, GM together with its Affiliates, Permitted Transferees or Member Group, as applicable, shall be deemed continuously to satisfy each minimum ten percent (10%) ownership requirement applicable to its rights under Section 4.6(c) , Section 5.2(a)(i) (subject to and in accordance with paragraph 3 herein), Section 5.4(b) and Section 7.7(e) through 7.7(g) of the LLCA and the definitions of “Specified Approval” and “Supermajority Approval” contained in the LLCA, notwithstanding any dilution of GM’s ownership interest in the Company. For the avoidance of doubt, any other conditions to the applicable rights and provisions remain unchanged (including the conditions set forth in Article VIII ), and no actual ownership percentage, voting weight, economic allocation, or distribution entitlement or priority is modified by this Agreement. 3. Board Representation. During the Protection Period, GM shall retain its appointment rights under Section 5.2 of the LLCA and shall be entitled to appoint, remove and replace at least one (1) voting GM Designee, notwithstanding (i) any dilution or reduction of GM’s ownership interest in the Company or (ii) Section 5.2(a)(iii) of the LLCA; provided that in the event the Proportionate Interests of GM (together with its Member Group) are reduced below ten percent (10%), GM shall have the right to appoint only one (1) GM Designee. For the avoidance of doubt, if GM (together with its Member Group) has Proportionate Interests of less than ten percent (10%) at any time outside the Protection Period, it shall not have the right to appoint a GM Designee to the Board of Directors and any GM Designee then serving shall be removed. 4. Drag-Along Rights. During the Protection Period, GM’s prior written consent shall be required for any exercise of rights under Section 10.4 of the LLCA, delivery of any Drag Along Right Exercise Notice or consummation of any Drag-Along Sale. Notwithstanding Section 10.4(c) or any other provision of the LLCA, during the Protection Period neither GM nor any GM Designee shall be required to consent to, vote in favor of or otherwise support any such exercise or sale unless GM has given that consent. 5. Member Meeting Quorum. During the Protection Period, a quorum under Section 4.5(b) of the LLCA shall require both the presence of an authorized representative of GM and the presence of Members holding at least seventy-five percent (75%) of the outstanding Units (including any Units held by GM and excluding any Non-Voting Units). Notwithstanding the foregoing, in the event that GM fails to attend any duly called meeting, quorum for the applicable rescheduled meeting duly called in accordance with Section 4.5(b) of the LLCA shall require only the presence of Members holding at least a majority of the outstanding Units (excluding any Non-Voting Units). Nothing in this Agreement limits the obligation of a Member to comply with the notice requirements or the requirements to obtain additional approvals for any matters set forth in Section 4.6 , in each case in accordance with Section 4.5(b) of the LLCA. 6. GM Capital Contribution Right. (i) Prior to the Protection Date, GM may, in its sole discretion, elect to make a cash Capital Contribution in exchange for the minimum number of additional Units (excluding Non-Voting Units) necessary to result in GM, together with its Affiliates, holding a Proportionate Interest of ten percent (10%) after giving effect to the contribution and all contemporaneous issuances and adjustments. GM shall exercise such right independently of any capital call, Approved Program and Budget or determination of funding need, by written notice to the Company and LAC (a “ Top-Up Notice ”). Page 2 (ii) Provided that the Protection Period has not expired or been earlier terminated, the Company shall provide GM and LAC with the Board of Directors’ proposed Fair Market Value of a Unit and reasonable supporting valuation and capitalization calculations no more than thirty (30) days prior to, and no less than ten (10) Business Days prior to, the Protection Date. Upon receipt of a Top-Up Notice from GM and the proposed Fair Market Value of a Unit from the Company, LAC and GM shall work to determine the Final FMV applicable to a Capital Contribution as of the date of the Top-Up Notice in accordance with the procedures set forth in the LLCA, including Section 3.6 of the LLCA; provided that, in the event that LAC and GM have not agreed to the Final FMV of a Unit (including Non-Voting Units, if applicable) in respect of such Capital Contribution within thirty (30) days following the Protection Date, then on any date following such thirty (30) day period and prior to the determination of Final FMV, either LAC or GM may refer the matter to an Independent Expert for determination in accordance with Section 13.10 of the LLCA. (iii) GM may withdraw its Top-Up Notice in writing at any time before funding is due. In the event that GM or its Affiliates Transfer any Units (other than a Transfer to an Affiliate) prior to funding, GM shall not be entitled to make a Capital Contribution pursuant to this paragraph 6 and the Top-Up Notice shall lapse without obligation to fund. Unless the Top-Up Notice is so withdrawn or lapsed, GM shall fund such Capital Contribution, and the Company shall concurrently issue the corresponding Units, promptly following the determination of Final FMV (and in any event, within ten (10) Business Days of such determination). (iv) The Company and LAC shall take all actions necessary to facilitate GM’s contribution and the corresponding issuance of Units in accordance with this paragraph 6, including obtaining any required approvals and updating Schedule “C” of the LLCA accordingly. Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in the LLCA, each of LAC and GM, in their respective capacities as a Member and, if applicable, Manager, irrevocably consents to GM’s contribution and the corresponding issuance of Units pursuant to the provisions of this paragraph for all purposes, including pursuant to Section 4.6 and Section 5.4 of the LLCA, and waives any applicable participation or preemptive rights with respect thereto (including any notice provisions applicable thereto), including pursuant to Section 3.3 through Section 3.5 of the LLCA. Notwithstanding Section 7.15 of the LLCA, no Management Catch-up Amount, matching or deemed contribution by LAC, or reallocation or cancellation of Units shall arise solely by reason of a contribution by GM pursuant to this paragraph 6. 7. Final FMV Determination. Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in the LLCA, in the event that LAC and GM have not agreed to the Final FMV of a Unit (including Non-Voting Units, if applicable) in respect of a Capital Contribution within ninety (90) days following any Capital Contributions made by LAC and its Permitted Transferees in advance of the determination of Final FMV in accordance with Section 3.3 of the LLCA, then on any date following such ninety (90) day period and prior to the determination of Final FMV, either LAC or GM may refer the matter to an Independent Expert for determination in accordance with Section 13.10 of the LLCA. 8. Effectiveness; Continuing Effect. This Agreement is effective as of the Effective Date and shall constitute an express amendment to the LLCA pursuant to Section 13.6 thereof. In the event of any conflict between this Agreement and the LLCA, this Agreement shall control (other than any conflict between this Agreement and Article VIII of the LLCA, which Article Page 3 VIII of the LLCA shall control). Except as expressly amended hereby, the LLCA is hereby ratified and confirmed and remains in full force and effect. Sections 13.3 , 13.9 , 13.11 , 13.18 and 13.19 of the LLCA are incorporated herein by reference, mutatis mutandis. This Agreement shall bind the signatories and their respective successors and permitted assigns. No amendment, supplement, or other modification, or waiver of rights under, this Agreement shall be valid unless made in writing and signed by each of the Parties. [ signature pages follow ] Page 4 Agreed and accepted: LITHIUM NEVADA VENTURES LLC By: Name: Title: GENERAL MOTORS HOLDINGS LLC By: Name: Title: LAC US CORP.
